chunks.title: Can I edit videos in this product?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I edit videos in this product?
Yes — in the **media/content module**. A video is a "content piece". First you need a video to edit: either
generate one with AI (from a brief → script → scenes) or import/upload your own clips. Then open the piece and
use the **Video timeline editor**: reorder/trim scenes, change transitions (cut/fade/crossfade), split or
delete a scene, refine a selected time-range with AI, and balance the **audio track** (voiceover + music
volume/duck) with a live waveform. Steps: open a content piece → "Timeline editor" → edit → Save.

chunks.title: Can I make a video with AI from just an idea/topic?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I make a video with AI from just an idea/topic?
Yes. In the content module, create a piece from a **brief** (a plain-language topic). The pipeline chains:
generate a **script** (beats) → **voiceover** (ElevenLabs) → **visuals** (per scene: AI video-gen via fal, or
images for a slideshow) → **assemble** into a real `.mp4` with ffmpeg. You approve cost/gates along the way
(the human accepts; the Conductor executes — single-writer). Without provider keys it still runs on
valid-shaped stubs so you can rehearse the flow.

chunks.title: Can I edit images?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I edit images?
Yes — the **image editor** in the media module (open an image asset on a content piece). It does brightness/
contrast/saturation, one-tap look filters (grayscale/sepia), a draggable text overlay, **crop + resize** to a
preset, and a **side-by-side compare** (original vs edited). The edit is exported as a NEW image asset
(non-destructive — the original stays).

chunks.title: Can I make longer videos (e.g. several minutes)?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I make longer videos (e.g. several minutes)?
Yes, via **scene decomposition**: the idea is split into N scenes that flow into each other (continuity
prompts), one AI-generated clip per scene, stitched with transitions. Video length ≈ number of scenes × per-
scene duration; the media budget is the practical cap. A duration target ("short / long") plans the number of
beats/scenes.

chunks.title: Can I refine just one part of a video (e.g. seconds 13–18)?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I refine just one part of a video (e.g. seconds 13–18)?
Yes — in the timeline editor, select a time-range and "Refine selection" with an instruction; only the covered
scene(s) are regenerated as a new version (the rest is untouched).

chunks.title: Can I add or balance audio (voiceover + background music)?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I add or balance audio (voiceover + background music)?
Yes — the timeline editor has an **audio track**: it shows a waveform for the voiceover and the music, with a
**voice-volume** slider and a **music-duck** slider. The saved mix is applied when the video is rendered
(voice + ducked music mixed into one track).

chunks.title: Can I generate a voiceover / music / sound effects?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I generate a voiceover / music / sound effects?
Yes — voiceover and SFX via **ElevenLabs**, music via **Suno**, all through the media providers. They attach
to a content piece as assets and feed the render.

chunks.title: Can I publish a video to YouTube or TikTok?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I publish a video to YouTube or TikTok?
Yes — connect the platform account first (content settings → connect), then on a finished (non-stub) render
click Publish and pick the platform. YouTube uses a resumable byte-upload; TikTok uses async status polling. A
publish only lands as "done" when the account is really connected; otherwise it is honestly marked as a stub.

## Design & Studio module

chunks.title: Can I design a UI theme / pick a style?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I design a UI theme / pick a style?
Yes — the **Designer module**. It has themes (colour palette, light+dark), styles (component language: radius/
shadow/fonts/density/motion — e.g. Apple, Material, Glassmorphic), animations, and typography. You can AI-
generate a theme/style from a brief, preview it live, pick from premade catalog entries, and "Use in project"
to apply it (it becomes the design-system context the coding agent follows).

chunks.title: Can I upload or customize my own theme/style?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I upload or customize my own theme/style?
Yes — duplicate a premade or generated theme, rename + edit its tokens, delete your own (premades are read-
only), and import/export a theme as JSON. Changes persist to your workspace.

## Dev-orchestration module (software projects)

chunks.title: Can I build software / a new project?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I build software / a new project?
Yes — the **dev module**. Create a project (link an existing git repo, or **greenfield** from a stack
template which initialises a real repo with a runnable seed file-tree). Tickets move across an AI pipeline
(refine → plan → implement → test → review); the code-writing agent runs in a Docker container. You approve;
the Conductor executes.

chunks.title: Can I preview or deploy my app?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I preview or deploy my app?
Yes — a per-ticket preview container, and persistent environments (dev/staging/prod). A **demo** environment
serves `main` at a stable URL and can auto-redeploy when main moves; a **prod build-export** produces a real
build tarball + fires a deploy-hook to an external server.

chunks.title: Can the AI ask me questions while working?
chunks.text:
Q: Can the AI ask me questions while working?
Yes — a stage can park on a **needs-input** question that surfaces as a structured approve/reject/choice card
(phone-usable). You answer; the parked turn resumes with your answer.

## Workspace-AI (the assistant)

chunks.title: What can the Workspace-AI assistant do?
chunks.text:
Q: What can the Workspace-AI assistant do?
It proposes actions from a plain-language request — create a ticket, create a content piece, move/assign
tickets, add a comment, or a multi-step plan — as a **proposal you accept** (it never writes state directly;
the Conductor is the single writer). It grounds on the workspace snapshot + your linked code (RAG) + (Q-fase)
the product's own capabilities.

chunks.title: Does the AI know my codebase / uploaded media?
chunks.text:
Q: Does the AI know my codebase / uploaded media?
Yes — the linked repo is indexed for retrieval (RAG), so the coding agent + the assistant ground on the actual
code; uploaded media becomes content assets the pipeline uses.

## Sources / knowledge / RAG

chunks.title: Can I give the AI extra context or docs?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I give the AI extra context or docs?
Yes — add **Sources** (context-docs, per-channel brand voice); they're indexed and injected into the relevant
AI stages. The repo is indexed on merge; you can re-scan the index.

## Accounts & channels

chunks.title: Can I manage multiple social accounts / channels?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I manage multiple social accounts / channels?
Channels carry a platform + brand voice; a content piece bound to a channel grounds its generation on that
channel's brand. Connecting and routing publishes to a specific account is what the account-management surface
provides.

chunks.title: In Fase 1 the control-API enqueues to an in-process serial Conductor; the Redis signal-log + lease land in Fase 2
chunks.text: ADR 0002: In Fase 1 the control-API enqueues to an in-process serial Conductor; the Redis signal-log + lease land in Fase 2. `CONTROL_API.md` (§3/§7) specifies that every user-initiated write goes: `_api` route → `preApiExecute` RBAC → **append a `WorkspaceSignal` to a Redis-backed serial signal-log** → the **single-instance Conductor** (running in the separate orchestrator process under `lease:orchestrator`) drains it and writes. That async signal-log + lease exists to keep the write path safe across the **web-app ↔ orchestrator process split** (the web-app scales horizontally; the orchestrator is single-instance). Fase 1 (basisplatform, no AI) ships the non-AI control-API ops (workspace/member/ RBAC/settings/board CRUD) BEFORE the orchestrator process exists — that process, its lease, the PTY/container engine, and the Redis drain loop are all Fase 2 (Lane A, spike-gated). If Fase 1 handlers enqueued to a Redis signal-log, nothing would drain it (no Conductor process yet) and nothing would persist. Decision: **In Fase 1 the control-API handler enqueues to an IN-PROCESS serial Conductor executor** (a single-writer promise-chain/mutex inside the one running web-app/dev process), which executes each op via `tenantDb` under `runInTenant(workspaceId)`. The **Redis-backed signal-log + `lease:orchestrator` + the out-of-process drain loop land in Fase 2** when the orchestrator process actually splits out (Lane A, A3). chunks.title: App-owned AES-256-GCM encryption for per-workspace secrets
chunks.text: ADR 0004: App-owned AES-256-GCM encryption for per-workspace secrets. Workspaces stores credentials it must replay to third parties — first the per-workspace GitLab token (`Workspace.gitlabTokenEnc`), later others. These cannot be one-way hashed (they must be decrypted to use) and must not sit in the DB as plaintext (B-07). The `@luckystack/secret-manager` resolves *deploy-time* env pointers at boot; it is not a per-row, per-tenant, runtime write-path for user-entered credentials, so it doesn't fit. Decision: Encrypt these secrets in the app with **AES-256-GCM**, in `server/crypto/secretBox.ts` (`encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret`), keyed by a single app key from `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` (any string, SHA-256-hashed to 32 bytes; resolved at boot like any env, so it can be a secret-manager pointer). Stored format is self-describing: `v1:<iv>:<tag>:<ct>` (base64). The **Conductor** is the only writer (B-23) — `gitlab-settings` encrypts on write; a Fase-2 GitLab client decrypts on use. When `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` is unset, secrets are stored `plain:<b64>` with a loud one-time boot warning. This keeps local dev frictionless while making the unencrypted state obvious + greppable; `decryptSecret` reads both forms, so setting the key later is non-breaking for new writes.

This decision was taken during an unattended overnight `/loop`: the AI can run tsc/lint/build + code-direct Mongo integration tests, but **cannot drive a browser**, so any Socket.io/`_sync` room-fanout + client-merge path is unverifiable this session. Investigation also showed the client room-join API (`joinRoom`) is not cleanly surfaced, and `sync.requireRoomMembership` defaults to `true` (0.2.0) — a `_sync` write path has moving parts that only a browser can prove. chunks.title: In-workspace writes broadcast a per-action `_sync` delta the client merges (no refetch)
chunks.text: ADR 0006: In-workspace writes broadcast a per-action `_sync` delta the client merges (no refetch). ADR 0005 split the write path into per-action typed `_api` routes but kept realtime as refetch-on-write, explicitly deferring the `_sync` delta layer to a browser-testable session ("This ADR is superseded if/when the `_sync` layer lands"). In practice the refetch model meant a user had to reload the board to see a new ticket ("ik moet een page refresh doen wat echt niet fatsoenlijk is") — realtime is a V1 requirement, and the user asked for **separate events per action** ("aparte events voor iedere verschillende actie"), with clients **merging deltas, never refetching**. The session now has agent-browser + Playwright MCP available, and the client room-join API (`joinRoom`/`leaveRoom` from `src/_sockets/socketInitializer`) + `syncRequest` / `useSyncEvents` are usable — the moving parts ADR 0005 flagged as unverifiable are now verifiable. Decision: **Every in-workspace write is a per-action `_sync` event that broadcasts its DELTA to the workspace room (room code = workspaceId); every client — including the sender — merges the delta into local state via `upsertSyncEventCallback`. No refetch.** - Each op keeps its OWN `_sync` route + event name (`workspaces/quickAdd`, `workspaces/bulkMove`, …) — the "separate events per action" ask. chunks.text: ADR 0007: Pluggable AI-provider layer — features resolve a backend at dispatch, never hardcode one. Workspaces integrates AI in many places: the Workspace-AI chat, docs generation, `.workspaces/Dockerfile` generation, the per-stage in-container coding agent, conflict resolution. The obvious path is to call the Claude CLI directly at each site (the P0.5 spike proved the subscription-billed interactive PTY works). The user requires instead that **each AI feature be independently assignable to a different backend** — Claude Code (CLI/PTY), a Gemini API key, or any future provider — chosen per feature. chunks.title: Container runtime model — clone-into-volume, name-based idempotency, off-chain provisioning
chunks.text: ADR 0008: Container runtime model — clone-into-volume, name-based idempotency, off-chain provisioning. Lane F's P1 scope is "L1 base image + provisioning skeleton" (`07b §1`). Building it surfaced concrete implementation choices the design doc (`07b`) frames but does not pin, and one it explicitly warns about (`§4`). This records the choices made in the phase-3 container spine, so a later session doesn't re-litigate them. Decision: - **Worktree = `git clone --single-branch` into a container-owned volume, NOT a bind-mount of the host `git worktree` checkout** (`07b §4`, Q-CT-WORKTREE). A git worktree's `.git` is a *gitdir pointer* back to the main repo; bind-mounting only the worktree dir leaves a dangling pointer that breaks git on the first command inside the container. The clone is self-contained. The `DEV-####` branch (cut at the frozen commit in phase 1b) is the clone's `--branch`, so its tip IS the frozen commit — no detaching checkout. - **`git config --system safe.directory '*'` is BAKED into L1.** The RO `/mirror` (host clone) is host-uid-owned; git's dubious-ownership guard refuses it. `-c safe.directory` is ignored by git for this key BY DESIGN — only system/global config is honored — so it must live in the image. - **Name-based idempotency, no persistence yet.** A container is keyed by `ws-<safe(workspaceId)>-<safe(ticketKey)>`; re-activation reuses/ restarts the named container. chunks.title: Register-flow AI operations — direct _api, draft-then-review, pure-context prompting
chunks.text: ADR 0009: Register-flow AI operations — direct _api, draft-then-review, pure-context prompting. Register-flow steps C (AI `.workspaces/Dockerfile`) and D (AI docs) are the first AI *write-ish* operations — each drives a slow `claude` turn (~30-120s) that produces a project artifact. Three cross-cutting choices settled while building them (phases 6a/6b). Decision: - **AI operations are direct `_api` routes, NOT Conductor control-ops.** `generateDockerfile` / `generateProjectDoc` / `aiChat` each run a multi-second-to-minute AI turn. The Conductor is the single SERIAL writer for authoritative state; routing a 2-minute turn through it would stall every other write. So AI ops call the provider layer directly from an `_api` handler (capability-gated), and only their *result* — if it mutates state — goes through a normal control-op (e.g. the Workspace-AI chat's accepted proposal dispatches `bulk-move`). - **Generated artifacts are a reviewable DRAFT, never auto-applied.** The Dockerfile is written to `data/workspaces/<id>/draft.Dockerfile` and validated to extend the L1 base (`FROM workspaces/base` only, Q-CT-DOCKERFILE-TRUST) — but NOT built or committed. The user reviews (Monaco slice) before it becomes the repo's `.workspaces/Dockerfile` and an L2 image. Docs land as `generated` InfoSources the user can see + toggle, not silent truth. - **Pure-context prompting.** The `claude-cli` provider runs in a scratch cwd (not a repo checkout), so AI-gen prompts pass the repo content inline

chunks.title: Per-container VS Code editor with a projected per-user profile (extensions + auth)
chunks.text: ADR 0010: Per-container VS Code editor with a projected per-user profile (extensions + auth). The V1 code editor is the real browser VS Code (openvscode-server), per [CODE_EDITOR.md] and the hybrid decision ([[workspaces-editor-plan]]): Monaco for lightweight embedded surfaces, openvscode-server for the full editor. An open question was *where* the full editor runs: - **Central editor + git worktrees** — one openvscode-server on the host that opens each ticket's worktree folder. Cheap, no per-ticket container for the editor, and extension logins persist for free (one shared user-data-dir). But the editor's LSP / "run" / integrated terminal only see the HOST toolchain, not the project's — so a Python/Go/… project gets no working IntelliSense, no in-project terminal, no per-project toolchain, unless the host happens to have every toolchain. - **Per-container editor** — openvscode-server INSIDE each ticket container (07b / [0008]). The editor sees exactly the project's L2 toolchain + installed deps + the agent's worktree, so LSP, "run", terminal, and extensions all work against the real project. Costs +300–800 MB/session and each container has its OWN filesystem, so extension installs + auth logins do NOT carry across tickets/workspaces by default. The user weighed both and chose the **per-container editor** (it is the better editor experience), **with the explicit requirement that the per-user editor storage — installed extensions AND auth tokens (secret storage) — is carried i

chunks.title: Git/workflow customization is split into structured per-workspace config vs skill/context-doc guidance, and the preview reverse-proxy is a pluggable Caddy/nginx provider
chunks.text: ADR 0011: Git/workflow customization is split into structured per-workspace config vs skill/context-doc guidance, and the preview reverse-proxy is a pluggable Caddy/nginx provider. Two related customization needs surfaced for Workspaces V1: 1. **Git/workflow** — teams name branches differently (`DEV-1240` vs `feature/DEV-1240-…`), have different push/MR policies, and want to steer *how* the AI commits ("split a ticket into testable steps, commit each passing step"). The runtime hardcoded `branch == ticket key` in three places (worktree, container, host). 2. **Preview hosting** — each ticket's container is exposed at a per-ticket subdomain of `workspace.<domain>` (wildcard DNS + cert). The user runs **nginx** today but Caddy is the easier fit for per-ticket route churn. An editor-specific Caddy driver already existed (`caddyRoutes.ts`), but nothing general or pluggable. The forces: the reverse proxy is an integration point (not core logic); branch/host derivation must be deterministic (code parses it); but "how to commit" is prose the AI interprets, not something code enforces. We needed a principled line so customization doesn't become a grab-bag. Decision: **A. The line = "does CODE act on it, or does the AI just READ it?"** - **Code acts → structured config.** A per-workspace `GitConfig` (`Workspace.gitConfig` JSON): `branchStrategy` (ticket-prefix | typed | custom template), `pushPolicy`, `targetBranch`, `protectedBranches`, `commitSigning`. `server/git/branchStrategy.ts`

chunks.title: The AI engine and a human's live editor never run on a ticket's container at once (edit-lock), and stale proxy routes self-heal on boot
chunks.text: ADR 0012: The AI engine and a human's live editor never run on a ticket's container at once (edit-lock), and stale proxy routes self-heal on boot. Two systems now touch a ticket's container + its `/work` git-worktree: - the **autonomous engine** (`stageRunner` drives an in-container `claude` turn that edits + commits on `/work`), and - the **per-ticket live editor** (openvscode-server, ADR 0010, edits the same `/work`). Running both at once races the worktree — the AI could commit on top of a human's unsaved edits, or vice-versa. `CODE_EDITOR_BUILD_PLAN` Track C4 (`userEditable` edit-lock) was schema-only and UNENFORCED. Separately, per-ticket proxy routes (`server/proxy`, ADR 0011) outlive a backend restart: after a crash/redeploy a `ws-route-*` can point at a container that is gone. The editor open-flow lives in another agent's files (`editorSession.ts`, `openEditor_v1.ts`); the engine + proxy are this side's. So the guard is built where it can be enforced without racing that work, and the editor-side half is offered as a ready helper to call. Decision: **A. Mutual edit-lock (`server/orchestrator/editGuard.ts`).** - **Engine side (enforced, `conductor.provisionContainers`):** before auto-running a stage turn, `isEditorRunning(workspaceId, ticketKey)` checks for a live openvscode-server process in the container; if present, the turn is **skipped + logged** (re-entering the stage re-triggers it). The engine never clobbers a human's open session. - **Editor side (`ticketEditGu

chunks.title: Engine control-plane completion — push-on-approval, pause/kill controls, off-chain realtime broadcast, and preview exposure
chunks.text: ADR 0013: Engine control-plane completion — push-on-approval, pause/kill controls, off-chain realtime broadcast, and preview exposure. The autonomous engine ran tickets to a committed branch, but the loop wasn't closed: the AI's work never left the container (commits were local-only), a runaway turn couldn't be stopped, the engine's stage-advance was silent (boards only updated on reload), and there was no way to see a ticket's app running. This ADR records the batch of control-plane decisions that close those gaps (CODE_EDITOR Track C/F + the realtime + preview layers), built engine/conductor/proxy-side while another agent built the editor/Caddy/UI side. Decision: **A. Push-on-approval (Track F) — `server/git/forge.ts`.** When a `done` turn leaves a stage that gates for approval OR is terminal, and the workspace `pushPolicy` ≠ `local-only`, push the ticket branch to origin and (for `merge-request`) open/find a GitLab MR against `targetBranch`. The GitLab token is decrypted ONLY in forge, injected transiently (git `withAuth` url + the MR `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header), never stored/logged; `protectedBranches` are refused. Fired fire-and-forget from the stage-runner so a slow/failed forge never breaks the turn. **B. chunks.title: Market-hardening — GitLab issue ingestion, a concurrent-turn CapacityManager, edge-auth on subdomains, and Sentry error tracking
chunks.text: ADR 0014: Market-hardening — GitLab issue ingestion, a concurrent-turn CapacityManager, edge-auth on subdomains, and Sentry error tracking. Toward market readiness, four gaps remained on the engine/proxy side: the board was NOT fed from the source (tickets came from quick-add, not GitLab issues — `gitlab-resync` was a no-op); nothing capped concurrent autonomous turns (runaway container spawning under load); the editor/preview subdomains were protected only by the openvscode connection token (no session gate); and error tracking was installed but inactive. This ADR records the batch closing them. Decision: **A. GitLab issue ingestion — `server/git/gitlabSync.ts` + the `gitlab-resync` op.** Pull the linked project's open issues via the GitLab REST API (reusing the forge token model: decrypt only here, `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header) and upsert them as tickets keyed `DEV-<iid>`. NEW issues enter at `unrefined` (the AI moves them on); EXISTING tickets get title/labels/description refreshed WITHOUT touching their pipeline position. The op broadcasts the touched tickets so the board updates live. This is the ingestion half of the loop (a webhook-driven continuous sync + a push-back of AI state to GitLab remain Fase-2 follow-ups). **B. CapacityManager — a host-wide concurrent-turn cap.** `provisionContainers` defers a turn (banner + broadcast, stays in-stage) when `busy worker AgentSessions >= WS_MAX_CONCURRENT_TURNS` (default 4). chunks.title: 0015-multi-instance-safety-deel-a
chunks.text: ADR 0015: 0015-multi-instance-safety-deel-a. The engine's authoritative-write path (the Conductor) was built single-instance: a global in-process promise chain (`chain`) serialised all writes, an in-process `Set` deduped re-sends, and the GitLab poller + editor reaper ran on `setInterval` in every process. Running 2+ instances behind the router would give: concurrent authoritative writes on the same workspace (races, double AI-turns on one container), un-deduped re-sends across instances, an unboundedly growing dedup Set, and N× duplicated background work. The user chose to do this RIGHT ONCE now — not because scale is here, but because the single-instance assumption is baked into the engine core and is far cheaper to remove now than to retrofit after more code depends on it. chunks.text: ADR 0016: Egress control on worker containers — an internal network + an allowlist forward proxy. A worker container runs code the AI writes plus a repo's dependencies — not fully trusted, and a single malicious npm/pip package can exfiltrate. Until now workers ran on the default bridge with FULL outbound network: they could POST secrets (env, the projected `~/.claude` creds, tokens) or the repo's code to any host, reach internal services, or abuse the host (mining/spam). That is the top blocker to letting customers trust their private code to the platform. Decision: Opt-in egress control (`WS_EGRESS=1`, default OFF ⇒ current behaviour unchanged). Domain-level, no MITM. chunks.text: ADR 0020: 0020-capacity-manager-hard-cap. Goal-item #12. The old CapacityManager (ADR 0014) was a **soft** cap: `provisionContainers` did `agentSession.count({ status: 'busy' }) >= MAX` and deferred above it. Between the count and `runStage`, N concurrent stage-activations all read the same "3 busy" and each start a 4th turn — a classic TOCTOU that a burst races straight past. Deferred tickets also only re-ran on a manual re-enter (no queue drain), so a backlog stalled until a human nudged it. And the user wants **hotfix/security tickets to force past the cap** (still needing approval to merge, #13's `priority=urgent` tier). N concurrent acquires can no longer all pass — the cap is hard. - **Urgent force-through:** `priority === 'urgent'` passes `force = true` — always admitted, but still tracked in the active set so normal tickets see true occupancy (an urgent turn does consume a real slot for everyone else). chunks.text: ADR 0022: 0022-crash-recovery-watchdog. Goal-item #1. chunks.text: ADR 0026: Observability — structured logging, metrics, health probes, flow insights. chunks.text: ADR 0035: Multi-project / multi-service workspaces (reverses D12 "one project per workspace"). chunks.text: ADR 0038: Deploy/CD — promote ladder + downloadable build export. B1 (ADR 0037) added persistent environments + `deployEnvironment`. B2 turns that into a CD flow: move a tested build UP the fixed `dev → staging → prod` ladder (gated), and let the user EXPORT a build to self-host elsewhere — the user's explicit ask: *"optie 1 [same-host deploy] maar we willen ook builds kunnen downloaden om die zelf ergens anders te hosten."* Decision: 1. **Promote ladder (`env-promote`).** `promoteEnvironment(project, service, fromKind, {approved})` deploys the next stage with the SOURCE env's EXACT image pinned (`deployEnvironment(..., {imageRef})`) — what you tested on dev is what ships, not a fresh branch pull. Gates: the source must be **live** (a health signal — you can't promote a broken build), and **prod requires an explicit approval** (B-23 confirm). The green-CI gate is a documented HOOK that C1 (BUILTIN_CI) fills — left as an explicit TODO in `promote.ts` rather than faking a check that doesn't exist yet. 2. **Downloadable build export (`build-export` + `BuildArtifact`).** `buildExport` runs `docker save` on the project's built image → an OCI tarball under the workspace data dir, tracked by a `BuildArtifact` row (building→ready|error) with an unguessable 24-byte `downloadToken` + a TTL. chunks.title: Built-in CI + quality gates (green/red blocking merge & promote)
chunks.text: ADR 0039: Built-in CI + quality gates (green/red blocking merge & promote). B2 (ADR 0038) left an explicit TODO: the prod-promote gate needs a green-CI check "once BUILTIN_CI lands". C1 un-defers `BUILTIN_CI_PIPELINES.md` (a designed-but-deferred spec) to build that: a CI job DAG on the existing orchestrator where a **red required job blocks merge/promote**. No CI models/parser/runner existed — only the two gate hooks I left (the `mr-merge` merge point + the prod-promote `ciGreen` TODO). Decision: 1. **Three models, exactly per BUILTIN_CI §9** — `Pipeline` (a project's `.workspaces/ci.yml` definition, one active per project), `PipelineRun` (one execution at a frozen commit; `status` gates), `PipelineJob` (one job = a container exec). ⚠ `Pipeline` is UNRELATED to `PipelineStage` (board columns) — same word, different concept; the schema carries a loud comment. 2. **"Borrowed, not built" runner** — `runPipeline` reads `.workspaces/ci.yml` at the frozen commit, parses it (a DEP-FREE parser — no js-yaml, which has no types + is a transitive-dep boot risk), creates the run + job rows, launches ONE job container via `launchTicketContainer` (same image/hardening/egress), runs each job's script via `docker exec` in stage order, records a `TicketEvent(type:'ci')` per job, and rolls up. No docker ⇒ `canceled` (never ran ⇒ does NOT gate red); no ci.yml ⇒ no run. 3. **The gate — default (A): gate + Admin override.** `ciGateForMr(mr, headSha)`: a red/running/stale run for the CURRENT head

chunks.title: Security & dependency scanning — first-class CI job types
chunks.text: ADR 0040: Security & dependency scanning — first-class CI job types. C1 (ADR 0039) built the CI runner + the merge/promote gates. C2 adds the user's ask: security + dependency scanning built DIRECTLY into the pipeline (not only via automation/cron or manual tickets). It inherits C1's runner/DAG entirely — the job TYPES are the delta. Decision: 1. **First-class scanner job types on the C1 runner** — a CI job gains a `type` (`script` default, plus `dep-audit` / `sca` / `secret-scan`). A scanner job needs NO `script` (its command comes from its type: `npm audit --json` for dep-audit; a credential-pattern `grep` for secret-scan). Results are PARSED into typed findings + a max severity (`server/ci/security.ts` pure parsers), stored on the `PipelineJob` (`severity`, `findings`) and rolled up to `PipelineRun.maxSeverity` — not freeform log-grepping. 2. **Fail policy: high/critical blocks a PROD promote; report-only on dev/merge.** A scanner job stays green (it doesn't fail the run — so it never hard-blocks merge), but its SEVERITY is a separate prod gate: `securityBlocksProdPromote(projectId)` blocks `env-promote → prod` (`promote.securityFindings`) when the latest run carries a high/critical finding. This matches "build it into the pipeline" without making a moderate advisory wedge every merge.

chunks.title: AI MR-review pass (propose→accept, never writes/approves)
chunks.text: ADR 0041: AI MR-review pass (propose→accept, never writes/approves). `BUILTIN_MR_REVIEW.md` designs an AI reviewer but marks it deferred, with a blanket "the AI never authors a review comment" posture. The SHIPPED schema, however, already widened `ReviewComment` for exactly this feature — `authorKind: 'user' | 'ai'` + optional `authorId`. C3 is the white-space item that fills it: an AI that reads an MR diff (RAG-grounded) and posts line-anchored findings — via propose→accept, never writing or approving directly. Decision: 1. **A non-coding `mr-review` AgentRole** (provider abstraction, ADR 0007 — new `AiFeature 'mr-review'`), mirroring the interviewer role. `run`: load the MR + `branchDiff` → `parseUnifiedDiff`, `retrieve()` the shared RAG for grounding, `runAiCompletion('mr-review', …)`, parse findings, and **validate every finding's line anchor against the real diff** (drop hallucinated line numbers). It emits ONE `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'mr-review')` carrying `{ mrId, findings[] }` in its `patch`. 2. **Propose→accept is the write boundary (B-23).** The AI NEVER writes a comment. On human accept, the `accept-suggestion` control-op dispatches a new `type === 'mr-review'` branch → the Conductor posts each finding as a real `ReviewComment(authorKind:'ai')` (no `authorId`). The AI never approves or merges — `mr-approve`/`mr-merge` stay human-only + approval-gated. This keeps the B-23 invariant intact at the write boundary while enabling an AI author on the comment. 3. **Reuse

chunks.title: AI-assisted rollback — root-cause role → propose→accept forward-revert + tracking ticket
chunks.text: ADR 0042: AI-assisted rollback — root-cause role → propose→accept forward-revert + tracking ticket. The forward-revert plumbing already exists (`mr-rollback` op → `rollbackMr` → `revertMergeCommit`, a history-preserving `git revert -m 1`, never a reset — invariant #7). The user wants an AI DRIVER on top: *"'X doet het niet meer' → AI figures out which changes likely caused it → rolls back → makes a ticket."* B3 adds that driver as a non-coding role, keeping the human in the loop for the actual revert (B-23). Decision: 1. **A non-coding `root-cause` AgentRole** (provider abstraction — new `AiFeature 'root-cause'`), mirroring the mr-review/interviewer roles. `run`: given a `symptom` + the recent merged MRs (newest first), `runAiCompletion('root-cause', …)` ranks the single most-likely culprit + explains why + what to verify. It parses `CULPRIT: <mr-number>` / `REASON: …` (pure `parseCulprit`), maps the number to the MR, and emits ONE `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'rollback', patch:{ mrId, symptom, reason })`. It NEVER reverts. 2. **Propose→accept is the write boundary (B-23).** On human accept, the `accept-suggestion` control-op dispatches a `type === 'rollback'` branch → `acceptRollback`: it runs the EXISTING `rollbackMr` (forward revert, invariant #7) on the ranked MR (best-effort — a no-op without a linked repo), then drafts a `DEV-####` tracking ticket pre-filled from the analysis (`labels:['rollback']`, high priority, the reason as the description, entering at `unrefined`), fi

chunks.title: User-app DB support + gated migrations
chunks.text: ADR 0043: User-app DB support + gated migrations. D1 gives a user's app a database surface: a read-only explorer + migration management. It ties to B1 environments (a migration targets an env's DB) and reuses the encrypted-secret path + the container/exec primitive. Greenfield — no DB model/op existed. Decision: 1. **`DbConnection` model** (per project, optionally per service/env; `kind` postgres/mysql/mongo; `urlEnc` ENCRYPTED via `secretBox`, never client-visible). The connection store the explorer + migrations resolve. 2. **Read-only explorer first (`introspectDb` / `db-introspect` op).** Lists a connection's tables/collections via a READ-ONLY listing query in a throwaway DB-client container (the base image has psql/mysql/mongosh). Browse-before-edit — the safest first cut. 3. **`Migration` model + gated apply (`db-migrate-apply` op).** A migration (`sql` + optional `rollbackSql`) is authored by the coding agent (schema-diff → SQL) and applied PER ENVIRONMENT as a control-op. Gates: **dev applies freely; prod requires an explicit approval AND a recorded rollback plan** (B-23 + the "prod apply = approval + backup/rollback" decision). Applied via the connection's DB client in a throwaway container; `status` tracks pending→applied/failed. The Conductor is the only applier (never client-side).

chunks.title: Reasoning first-class — per-stage think-budget (surfaced) + plan-critique gate
chunks.text: ADR 0044: Reasoning first-class — per-stage think-budget (surfaced) + plan-critique gate. E1 makes reasoning first-class: (1) a per-stage think-budget (reasoning effort / max-turns / auto-escalate) and (2) a plan-critique gate — an adversarial pass that attacks the plan before implement. Decision: 1. **Think-budget is ALREADY surfaced — no new work.** The per-stage `modelCfg` (`StageModelChoice`: `model`/`effort` low→max/`maxTurns` + `autoEscalate` + escalation `rules`) is editable in the pipeline page today (`src/workspaces/pipeline/page.tsx` — the effort `Segmented` + the turns input + the auto-escalate rules). E1 confirms this is the think-budget primitive; it needs no change. 2. **Plan-critique gate = a new adversarial role.** A non-coding `plan-critique` AgentRole (provider abstraction, `AiFeature 'plan-critique'`) reads a ticket's plan (the latest `CarryOver` envelope's `summary` + `openQuestions`) and attacks it — what's missing / what breaks / which assumption is risky — emitting a `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'plan-critique')` the human folds in before implement. It's read-only + advisory (no auto-apply); it runs through the suggestion/feed, **never a second AI window**. Triggered by a `plan-critique` control-op (a pipeline can call it after the plan stage, optional gate).

chunks.title: RAG sharpen — institutional memory + wire into surfaces + re-index on merge
chunks.text: ADR 0045: RAG sharpen — institutional memory + wire into surfaces + re-index on merge. The RAG index is already SINGULAR — one `RagEntry` store, one `retrieve()`, one embedder (`server/rag/{index,embed}.ts`). An earlier fix grounded the Workspace-AI chat. E2 finishes the wiring: consumption breadth + institutional memory, all on the same index (no parallel store). Decision: 1. **Institutional memory on the same store.** `server/rag/memory.ts` indexes the workspace's `Handoff` (summary/decisions/gotchas/next) + `CarryOver` (summary/open-questions) envelopes into `RagEntry` under a reserved sentinel commit `institutional-memory`. `retrieveMemory()` reuses the single `retrieve()` with that sentinel — so prior learnings surface via the SAME retrieval path, no second index. Frozen- per-"commit" replace (mirrors code indexing). Un-defers `additions/03_institutional_memory`. 2. **Incremental re-index on merge.** A successful `mr-merge` fires a best-effort re-index of the code RAG (the target branch advanced) + the institutional memory — off the caller's path, never blocking the merge. Previously re-index was manual-only ("Reindex code"). 3. **Wire retrieval into more surfaces.** The plan-critique role (E1) now grounds its critique in `retrieveMemory()` — repeated past mistakes become the highest-value gaps. (The C3 mr-review role already grounds on `retrieve()`.) An `index-memory` control-op (re)builds the memory on demand.

chunks.title: Greenfield scaffolding — curated stack templates + project-from-template
chunks.text: ADR 0046: Greenfield scaffolding — curated stack templates + project-from-template. F1 adds "create a NEW project from a stack template" — the GENERATE side of the GENERATE-vs-LINK split (features/01). `additions/04` covers onboarding an EXISTING repo; F1 covers a fresh one, plus a welcome flow. It builds on A1's multi-project model (a template creates a project) + the project-create/default- pipeline path. Decision: 1. **A small CURATED template catalog** (`server/scaffold/templates.ts`) — a few reviewed stacks (node-api, react-vite, python-fastapi), each carrying the seed config a fresh project needs: a base image hint, a dev command, and starter convention docs. Pure data + `listTemplates()`/`getTemplate()`. A cross-workspace template marketplace is later (features/01 B-O4). 2. **`project-from-template` control-op** — creates a fresh `Project` (reusing the A1 project model) with the template's `devCommand`/`baseImageRef`, seeds the template's starter convention docs as `InfoSource(source:'starter')` (visible in Sources, injectable into the coding agent — the starter-doc pattern), and seeds the project's own default pipeline (`createDefaultPipeline`). The catalog is exposed in the snapshot (`templates[]`) for the picker. 3. **Welcome flow — the data + method are wired; the wizard UI is a follow-up.** `templates` + `createFromTemplate` are on the context; a first-run wizard on top of the existing setup steps is the remaining UX layer (a picker rendering `templates[]` → `crea

chunks.title: Delivery analytics — on-request fold over the append-only log (tokens, not €)
chunks.text: ADR 0047: Delivery analytics — on-request fold over the append-only log (tokens, not €). G1 un-defers PRODUCT_ANALYTICS: cycle-time, throughput, stuck-points, and token-cost-by-type, folded over the append-only `TicketEvent` + `SpendRecord`/usage log. The `computeInsights` fold already exists (avgCycle/throughput/avgTokens); G1 adds the fuller analytics + a dashboard surface. Cost in TOKENS, not € (invariant #9 — the parked price-blocking). Decision: 1. **A PURE on-request fold — no new write path/model/verb** (`server/obs/analytics.ts` `computeAnalytics`). It folds tickets + the already-aggregated usage into: cycle-time **p50/p85** (p85 = the robust "how long does it really take", not a mean skewed by outliers), **weekly throughput** (4 buckets), **stuck-points** (tickets parked in stuck/paused/needs-input), and **token cost by label** (cost per work TYPE). `now` is injected → deterministic + unit-testable. Advisory — it gates nothing. 2. **Surfaced on the Usage page** — the snapshot emits `analytics` (alongside the existing `insights`); the Usage page renders a "Delivery analytics" card (p85/stuck/weekly stat cards + a throughput bar chart + a tokens-by-type list). No new page/route.

chunks.title: Review ergonomics — cross-ticket answer-queue + presence soft-claim
chunks.text: ADR 0048: Review ergonomics — cross-ticket answer-queue + presence soft-claim. G2 un-defers additions/05 + 06: a cross-ticket **answer-queue** (drain every pending question from one place, phone-first) + **presence/claim** (who's viewing/answering + a soft-claim so two reviewers don't double-answer). The presence relay already exists (`_sync/presence`, ephemeral who's-viewing). Decision: 1. **Answer-queue = a snapshot-derived cross-ticket view.** Every ticket parked on a question (`Ticket.needsInput` set, or status `needs-input`) surfaces in `snapshot.answerQueue` (`ticketKey`, `title`, `question`, `priority`), highest-priority first — one queue the reviewer swipes/stacks through instead of hunting per-ticket. Pure derivation over the existing tickets — no new write path/model. 2. **Soft-claim on the presence relay.** The presence event gains a `claiming` flag: a reviewer answering a ticket broadcasts `{viewing:true, claiming:true}`; the client renders "X is answering" and can disable the answer input for others. Ephemeral + idempotent (like viewing) — the authenticated user id comes from the session (unspoofable), the socket room fan-out makes it multi-instance-safe for free. NOT authoritative state (no Conductor write) — it's a coordination hint, not a lock.

chunks.title: Content-platform pivot — Workspaces as an all-in-1 AI content platform on the shared engine
chunks.text: ADR 0049: Content-platform pivot — Workspaces as an all-in-1 AI content platform on the shared engine. Workspaces began as an AI **dev-orchestration** environment (tickets → pipeline → coding agent, human-in-the-middle). With the Studio marketing module (ADR 0033) it became clear the product is really an **all-in-1 tool for using AI in many ways**. The user wants to add AI **content creation** as a first-class use: short + long-form video, reference-driven photorealistic imagery, avatars, music, 3D, auto-posting to platforms, and animated software demos — driven by the same "user approves, the engine executes" model. This is a deliberate scope expansion the user wants; the question was whether it fits the architecture. It does — as an **addition, not a rewrite**. Decision: **Add a content lane on the existing engine.** A `projectType` (`dev` | `content` | …) selects the workflow lane; the same Conductor, realtime, RBAC, RAG, cron/automation, control-ops and B-23 single-writer serve both. Content is NOT a separate product — one app, distinct workflow surfaces. Concretely: 1. **The pipeline engine is generic.** A content-pipeline (idea → script → generate → assemble → review → publish) is just different stage-configs + roles on the same stage-runner. 2. **The provider abstraction (ADR 0007) is the "one tool for everything"** — our tool is the router, not a single external vendor. Default gateway **Fal.ai** (image/video/3d) + **ElevenLabs** (voice) + **Remotion** (code-driven as

chunks.title: Content-platform data model — projectType lane + 9 content models (F0.1)
chunks.text: ADR 0050: Content-platform data model — projectType lane + 9 content models (F0.1). First item of `CONTENT_PLATFORM_PROGRAM.md` (ADR 0049) — schema-first. The content lane needs its data model published before any engine/client work. Decision: 1. **A `projectType` on Project** (`'dev'` | `'content'`, default `'dev'`) selects the workflow lane. Zero migration for existing projects (default). 2. **Nine content models**, all tenant-scoped by **explicit `workspaceId` filtering** (NOT the `tenantDb` `$extends` auto-scoping): `Channel` (distribution target + house style), `ContentProject` (a content piece flowing the pipeline — `stageId`/`status` mirror Ticket so the generic stage-runner drives it), `ContentAsset` (a produced media asset), `Script` + `Beat` (narration + storyboard), `MediaJob` (async generation to a provider, `costCents` metered), `RenderJob` (Remotion assembly), `StylePreset` (a named style, `workspaceId` null = global default / set = per-workspace), `MediaSpend` (the €-cost ledger, cents). 3. **Media cost in CENTS** on `MediaJob`/`RenderJob`/`MediaSpend` — metered real-money €, distinct from the coding-agent token accounting (invariant #9).

chunks.title: Media €-budget + pre-generation guard (F0.2)
chunks.text: ADR 0051: Media €-budget + pre-generation guard (F0.2). Media APIs (Fal/Veo/ElevenLabs/3d) are **metered real-money** per generation — unlike the coding agent, which runs on the Max subscription and is accounted in tokens (invariant #9). A cron-driven content loop could run up a real bill, so a per-workspace **€-cap + pre-generation guard** is needed before any generation lands. Decision: 1. **A `MediaBudget` model** — ONE row per workspace (`@@unique workspaceId`), `capCents`/`spentCents`/`alertPct`/`enabled`, opt-in (disabled by default). Cents (Int) — no float money. 2. **A pure guard `checkMediaBudget(prisma, ws, costCents)`** (`server/media/budget.ts`) → `{ ok, reason?, unlimited, capCents, spentCents, remainingCents }`. No budget / `!enabled` / `capCents<=0` = **unlimited** (always ok). Over cap → `ok:false, reason:'media.budgetExceeded'`. Pure read; the caller records on success. `recordMediaSpend(...)` writes the `MediaSpend` €-ledger row + debits `spentCents`. `getMediaBudgetStatus(...)` exposes the status (incl. `overAlert`) for the settings UI + snapshot. 3. **The budget is set via an `edit-media-budget` control-op** (B-23 write path) — capability `workspaceSettings`, Conductor upserts the row. The user never writes the budget directly.

chunks.title: Media provider abstraction + stub adapters (F0.3)
chunks.text: ADR 0052: Media provider abstraction + stub adapters (F0.3). The content lane generates ASSETS (images/video/voice/…), not text. The existing AI-provider abstraction (ADR 0007, `server/ai/*`) is text-completion-shaped (`AiCompletionResult.text`). Media needs the same *pattern* (features resolve to a provider; no feature hardcodes a backend) but a different *result shape* (an asset + a metered € cost). No API keys exist yet — the whole pipeline must run on dummy data. Decision: 1. **A parallel MEDIA layer** in `server/media/` mirroring `server/ai/`: `MediaFeature` (`image-gen`, `reference-image`, `video-gen`, `tts`, `music`, `sfx`, `avatar`, `model-3d`), `MediaProviderId` (`fal`, `elevenlabs`), `MediaGenerationRequest`/`Result` (asset + `costCents` + `stub` flag), `MediaProvider` interface, `DEFAULT_MEDIA_ASSIGNMENTS` + `resolveMediaAssignment` (per-workspace override seam), and `runMediaGeneration(req, overrides)` dispatch. 2. **Registry-level STUB fallback.** Each adapter's `available()` is false until its key env is present; when unavailable, `runMediaGeneration` returns a valid-SHAPED stub asset (`stub://<kind>/<feature>/<style>`) + a realistic declared `costCents` (video » image » voice). So the entire content pipeline runs end-to-end on dummy data, and the €-budget guard (F0.2) is exercised — without any keys. 3. **`reference-video-analysis` stays a TEXT `AiFeature`** on `gemini-api` (extends `server/ai` union + `DEFAULT_ASSIGNMENTS`) — it returns a beat/style BLUEPRINT

chunks.title: Cross-cutting style/preset system (F0.4)
chunks.text: ADR 0053: Cross-cutting style/preset system (F0.4). ADR 0049 makes styles a first-class, cross-cutting concept: every AI feature (text or media) composes a generation from `feature + input + style + free-form extra instructions`. A style is a curated system-prompt preset (e.g. `realistisch`, `cinematic`), with global defaults + per-workspace (brand) overrides. The `StylePreset` model exists (F0.1); F0.4 builds the resolve/compose/seed logic + the write path. Decision: 1. **`server/content/styles.ts`** — `ensureDefaultStyles` (idempotent seed of the global `builtin` styles, `workspaceId=null`), `resolveStyle(prisma, ws, feature, key)` (a per-workspace style with the same key WINS over the global; no key/no match → null), `composeStylePrompt(style, extra)` (style system-prompt + free-form extra instructions, joined), and `listStyles` (global + workspace, the workspace shadowing the global — for the picker UI). 2. **Per-workspace styles are written via a `save-style` control-op** (B-23; capability `workspaceSettings`; Conductor upserts by `(workspace, feature, key)`). Global styles are seed-only (`builtin`, not user-writable). 3. **Styles thread into gen at the CALL SITE, not into `runAiCompletion`'s signature.** The content pipeline (F1.x) resolves the style + composes the system prompt, then passes it as `req.system` (text) or `MediaGenerationRequest.style` (media). No feature signature changes.

chunks.title: Generic content-pipeline — fixed stage sequence + control-ops (F1.1)
chunks.text: ADR 0054: Generic content-pipeline — fixed stage sequence + control-ops (F1.1). A content piece (`ContentProject`) must flow through a workflow the way a Ticket flows through the dev board. F1.1 builds that engine: the stage sequence + the control-ops that drive a piece through it (the per-stage generation wires in F1.2–F1.5). Decision: 1. **A FIXED ordered content-stage sequence** (`server/content/pipeline.ts`): `idea → script → generate → assemble → review → publish`, with `nextContentStage`/`isContentStage` helpers. Unlike the dev board (per-project `PipelineStage` rows), the content stages are a code constant — the sequence is uniform across content pieces (per-stage CONFIG comes later, F4). 2. **Three control-ops** (B-23; capability `workTickets`): `content-create` (make a `ContentProject` at `idea`), `content-advance` (→ an explicit `toStage`, else the next stage; past `publish` → `status:done`), `content-archive` (soft). The **Conductor is the only writer** of `stageId`/`status`. 3. **`project-create` gains `projectType`** — `projectType:'content'` makes a content-lane project (NO board pipeline seeded); default stays `dev` (a board + its `PipelineStage`s). Zero change for existing dev flows.

chunks.title: Content script + beats generation with a stub fallback (F1.2)
chunks.text: ADR 0055: Content script + beats generation with a stub fallback (F1.2). The `script` stage turns a brief into a narration Script + storyboard Beats (each beat carries a `visualPrompt` that drives the per-beat image in F1.4). Script generation is text, so it uses the text AI abstraction (`runAiCompletion`) — but that has NO stub fallback (unlike the media registry, F0.3), and no keys exist. So with no key it would return `ai.providerUnavailable` and the pipeline would stall. Decision: 1. **A content-script service `server/content/script.ts`** — `generateScript(prisma, { workspaceId, contentProjectId, brief, styleKey?, extraInstructions? })` resolves the `script` style + composes the system prompt (F0.4), calls `runAiCompletion('script', …)`, then writes a `Script` + ordered `Beat` rows and returns `{ scriptId, beatCount, stub, providerId }`. 2. **A CONTENT-LOCAL stub fallback.** When the provider is unavailable (no key), `generateScript` produces a valid-shaped 4-beat script from the brief (dummy-data mode) — the stub lives in the content layer, NOT in `runAiCompletion`, so the global text abstraction (incl. the coding agent) never silently stubs. 3. **`script` is a text `AiFeature`** (default `gemini-api` — non-coding bulk text, overridable). The `Script` records the resolved `providerId` + links the resolved `styleId`. 4. **Driven by a `content-gen-script` control-op** (B-23, `workTickets`) — the Conductor calls `generateScript` for the piece.

chunks.title: Voiceover generation — metered path + per-beat timing (F1.3)
chunks.text: ADR 0056: Voiceover generation — metered path + per-beat timing (F1.3). The `generate` stage turns a Script into a voice asset. This is the first item to run the FULL metered media path end-to-end (budget-check → media gen → asset + spend), and it must produce the per-beat timing the montage (F1.5) needs to align visuals to the narration. Decision: 1. **`server/content/voice.ts` `generateVoiceover`** runs the whole path: `estimateMediaCostCents('tts')` → `checkMediaBudget` (block BEFORE the paid call) → `runMediaGeneration({feature:'tts', …})` (stub when no key) → a voice `ContentAsset` + a `MediaJob` (linked `resultAssetId`) → `recordMediaSpend`. Returns `{ ok, blocked?, assetId, costCents, stub, totalMs }`. 2. **Budget-check BEFORE gen, via `estimateMediaCostCents`** — a new registry export returning the expected cost so the guard runs before the (paid) call; the actual `result.costCents` is recorded after. A cap hit returns `blocked:true` and runs no gen. 3. **Per-beat timing** — each `Beat` gets a persisted `durationMs` (word-count-derived, min 1.5s), and the voice asset's `metadata` carries `{ totalMs, timing[] }` (cumulative start + duration per beat). Deterministic → testable.

chunks.title: Per-beat image generation (F1.4)
chunks.text: ADR 0057: Per-beat image generation (F1.4). Each storyboard `Beat` needs a visual for the montage. F1.4 generates one image per beat via `image-gen` (stub, no key), in the chosen style + extra instructions, and links it on the beat. Decision: `server/content/images.ts` `generateBeatImages` loops the script's beats: per beat it budget-checks (`estimateMediaCostCents('image-gen')` → `checkMediaBudget`), runs `runMediaGeneration({feature:'image-gen', prompt: beat.visualPrompt})`, writes a `MediaJob` + an image `ContentAsset`, links `Beat.imageAssetId`, and records the spend. It **stops early (partial result) if the budget cap is hit** mid-loop. Driven by the `content-gen-images` control-op (B-23, `workTickets`).

chunks.title: Assembly / render — the complete downloadable output (F1.5)
chunks.text: ADR 0058: Assembly / render — the complete downloadable output (F1.5). The final `assemble` stage composes a piece's beats (+ their images) + the voiceover into the COMPLETE downloadable output. This closes Fase 1 — the content pipeline produces a finished asset end-to-end. No keys, so the render is a stub; the render itself is Remotion (local CPU), not a metered API. Decision: 1. **`server/content/assembly.ts` `assembleContent`** builds a Remotion timeline (`{ order, text, imageAssetId, durationMs }` per beat, over the voice asset, `totalMs` summed), writes a `RenderJob` (`composition:'faceless'`, `status:'done'`), and produces the final `ContentAsset` (`kind:'render'`, `metadata.downloadable=true` + `hasVoice`/`hasAllImages`/`beatCount`/`totalMs`), linking `RenderJob.resultAssetId`. 2. **Local render is FREE (`costCents:0`)** — Remotion renders on CPU, not a metered media API, so it does NOT debit the €-budget (only the gen calls do: voice + images). This keeps the cost model honest. 3. **The render asset IS the deliverable** — its `stub://render/<piece>` url + `downloadable` flag is the complete output the user downloads + posts manually (the primary near-term path). A real HTTP download route is F3.3. 4. Driven by the `content-assemble` control-op (B-23, `workTickets`).

chunks.title: Reference-driven photorealistic image generation (F2.1, #1 feature)
chunks.text: ADR 0059: Reference-driven photorealistic image generation (F2.1, #1 feature). The user's #1-priority feature: generate an image CONDITIONED on a reference image, in a chosen style (realism first) + free-form extra instructions (e.g. "dancing, brown curly hair"). The `reference-image` media feature exists (F0.3); F2.1 wires the content-side flow. Decision: `server/content/referenceImage.ts` `generateReferenceImage` runs the metered path: `checkMediaBudget('reference-image')` → `runMediaGeneration({feature:'reference-image', referenceUrl, style, extraInstructions})` (stub) → an image `ContentAsset` (`metadata.hasReference`) + a `MediaJob` (records the `referenceUrl` + `styleId`) → `recordMediaSpend`. **The style defaults to `realistisch`** unless overridden (realism is the priority). Driven by the `content-gen-reference-image` op (B-23, `workTickets`), which requires a `referenceUrl`.

chunks.title: Short-form clip generation (F2.2)
chunks.text: ADR 0060: Short-form clip generation (F2.2). A short-form (TikTok/Shorts/Reels) clip is a single hook-driven vertical video, distinct from the assembled faceless-explainer. F2.2 generates it via `video-gen` (stub) with a hook + captions. Decision: `server/content/shortForm.ts` `generateShortForm` runs the metered path (`checkMediaBudget('video-gen')` → `runMediaGeneration({feature:'video-gen'})` stub → video `ContentAsset` + `MediaJob` + spend), derives a `hook` + `captions` from the prompt (stub; a live hook-writer lands with keys), and stores them on the asset metadata (`format:'short'`). Driven by `content-gen-shortform` (B-23, `workTickets`, requires a `prompt`).

chunks.title: Reference-video analysis → blueprint that seeds a script (F2.3)
chunks.text: ADR 0061: Reference-video analysis → blueprint that seeds a script (F2.3). The user wants to "mimic another video's storytelling/pacing/style over a NEW story". F2.3 analyses a reference video (multimodal, Gemini) into a beat/style BLUEPRINT and retells a new story in that shape. Decision: `server/content/referenceVideo.ts` `analyzeReferenceVideo` calls the `reference-video-analysis` text AiFeature (Gemini, video-capable), producing a `VideoBlueprint` (`pacing`, `styleHint`, `beats[]`), then SEEDS a `Script` (title "From reference video") + `Beat`s from it — the NEW story in the reference's shape. Content-local stub (no key). Driven by `content-analyze-reference-video` (B-23, `workTickets`, requires `referenceVideoUrl` + `newStory`).

chunks.title: Shared single-asset gen + avatar (F2.4)
chunks.text: ADR 0062: Shared single-asset gen + avatar (F2.4). Avatar/music/sfx/3d are simple "prompt (+ style) → one asset" gens with identical plumbing (budget → gen → asset → spend). F2.4 builds the shared helper + wires avatar; F2.5/F2.6 reuse it. Decision: `server/content/mediaAsset.ts` `generateMediaAsset(prisma, { feature, prompt?, referenceUrl?, styleKey?, extraInstructions? })` is the generic metered path for the simple single-asset features. The 4 ops (`content-gen-avatar`/`-music`/`-sfx`/`-3d`, B-23, `workTickets`) share ONE Conductor case that maps op→`MediaFeature` and calls it. The specialised services (voice timing, per-beat images, short-form captions, reference-image) keep their own files.

chunks.title: Music + SFX generation (F2.5)
chunks.text: ADR 0063: Music + SFX generation (F2.5). The montage benefits from a soundtrack + sound effects. F2.5 adds music + sfx gen — both simple single-asset gens, so they reuse the shared `generateMediaAsset` path (F2.4). Decision: Music + sfx generation ride the `content-gen-music` / `content-gen-sfx` ops (already wired in F2.4's shared Conductor case → `generateMediaAsset` with feature `music`/`sfx`). Both default to the ElevenLabs adapter (stub, no key). Music (Suno) gets a dedicated provider later; for now it routes to the voice adapter's stub.

chunks.title: 3D-concepting generation (F2.6)
chunks.text: ADR 0064: 3D-concepting generation (F2.6). 3D is the weakest modality (concepting-grade, not hero assets) + lowest priority (ADR 0049). F2.6 adds it as a simple single-asset gen on the shared path — closing Fase 2 (all modalities present). Decision: 3D generation rides the `content-gen-3d` op (wired in F2.4's shared Conductor case → `generateMediaAsset` with feature `model-3d`, default fal/Meshy-class provider, stub). No new engine code.

chunks.title: Publishing behind the B-23 approval gate + YouTube (F3.1)
chunks.text: ADR 0065: Publishing behind the B-23 approval gate + YouTube (F3.1). Posting to a real channel is irreversible + public — the exact case B-23 reserves for an explicit human confirm. F3.1 builds publishing behind that gate, with a platform-adapter abstraction + a YouTube adapter (dummy, no key). Decision: 1. **`content-request-publish` creates a publish SUGGESTION** (`WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'publish', patch:{contentProjectId, assetId, platform})`) — it does NOT post. Accepting it (`accept-suggestion` → the new `'publish'` branch) makes the **Conductor** call `publishAsset` (the only writer of the `PublishJob`). The AI never publishes. 2. **A platform abstraction** (`server/content/publish.ts`) with `BUILT_PLATFORMS` (youtube, tiktok) + `FUTURE_PLATFORMS` (instagram, linkedin). A built platform with no key → a **dummy post** returning a `stub://<platform>/<asset>` external url; a future-ready platform → a `PublishJob(status:error, error:'platform.notBuilt')` (recorded, not posted). 3. **A `PublishJob` model** records each post (platform, status, externalUrl, error).

chunks.title: TikTok publishing + IG/LinkedIn future-ready (F3.2)
chunks.text: ADR 0066: TikTok publishing + IG/LinkedIn future-ready (F3.2). F3.2 adds TikTok posting (same B-23 gate) + registers Instagram/LinkedIn as future-ready (not built now). Decision: TikTok is in `BUILT_PLATFORMS` (established in F3.1's abstraction) — it posts via the same gate + `publishAsset` (dummy, no key). Instagram + LinkedIn stay in `FUTURE_PLATFORMS`: a publish request for them records a `PublishJob(error:'platform.notBuilt')` — visible, never a silent post. No new engine code beyond F3.1's abstraction.

chunks.title: Content automation + conversational entry (F3.3)
chunks.text: ADR 0067: Content automation + conversational entry (F3.3). Two entry modes for content (ADR 0049): recurring channel automation (cron) + a conversational quick-start (the Assistant spins up a piece from a brief). F3.3 wires both, reusing the automation engine (ADR 0027) + the content pipeline (F1.1). Decision: 1. **A schedulable `content-ideator` AgentRole** (`server/content/ideatorRole.ts`, `mutates:true`). A cron trigger (`action:'invoke-agent-role', params:{role:'content-ideator', theme?}`) fires it; because it `mutates`, the automation executor GATES it into an approval suggestion — it never writes content directly (B-23). Registered at boot in `server.ts`. 2. **A `content-from-brief` op** (B-23, `workTickets`) — the conversational quick-start: creates a content-lane `Project` + a first `ContentProject` piece from a chat brief in one op (on the user's accept). This is what the Assistant calls to "spin up a video about startup A".

chunks.title: Main-navbar grouping (F4.1)
chunks.text: ADR 0068: Main-navbar grouping (F4.1). The main nav rail is a flat list of 11 items — the user asked to declutter it with better GROUPING + a contextual secondary navbar, plus lazy-loading for bundle size. F4.1 delivers the grouping (the highest-value, lowest-risk part) now; the richer per-area secondary navbar + lazy-loading are scoped follow-ups (they need browser verification, which is deferred with no keys/running server). Decision: Each `NavDef` gets a `group` (`work` | `build` | `studio` | `insights`); the rail renders items grouped under section headers (expanded) or thin dividers (collapsed), in `GROUP_ORDER`. Group labels render via a variable (`GROUP_LABELS[g]`), matching the existing nav's variable-rendered `it.label` (no new i18n debt; consistent with the current pattern). Theme tokens only (`text-disabled`, `bg-divider`).

chunks.title: Content lane in the snapshot (F4.2)
chunks.text: ADR 0069: Content lane in the snapshot (F4.2). The content UI + settings need the content state on the client. F4.2 wires the content lane into the workspace snapshot (the testable, enabling core); the rich page components + the settings FORM are the browser-deferred layer (no keys / running server for a visual pass). Decision: The snapshot gains `content: ContentSnapshot` — `pieces` (the non-archived `ContentProject`s: id/title/format/stageId/status/channelId) + `mediaBudget` (the `getMediaBudgetStatus` fold: enabled/cap/spent/alert/overAlert). Content models scope by explicit `workspaceId` (via `currentWorkspaceId()` inside `runInTenant`), matching the feature-model pattern (ADR 0050) — NOT `tenantDb` (content isn't in `TENANT_MODELS`). Threaded through `WorkspacesProvider` + `WorkspacesContext` so any content surface reads `content` from context.

chunks.title: AI-drives-UI copilot — propose a directive, never write (F4.3)
chunks.text: ADR 0070: AI-drives-UI copilot — propose a directive, never write (F4.3). The user wants the AI to steer the app (navigate + pre-fill forms) for a good UX — but B-23 forbids LLMs writing authoritative state, and literal pixel-clicking of our own UI is an anti-pattern (ADR 0049). F4.3 builds the copilot as a PROPOSAL model: the Assistant proposes a UI directive; the client applies the navigate/pre-fill guidance; the user confirms the underlying control-op (the Conductor writes). Decision: A `copilot-propose` op (B-23, `workTickets`) creates a `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'copilot', patch:{navigate, prefill, op})` — the UI directive: WHERE to navigate, WHAT to pre-fill a form with, and the underlying control-op the user would confirm. The copilot **writes nothing authoritative** — only the proposal. The client (browser-deferred) reads it, navigates + pre-fills, and the user taps the real control-op (which the Conductor executes). This is "AI drives, human confirms".

chunks.title: Per-channel brand-RAG + content-analytics (F5.1)
chunks.text: ADR 0071: Per-channel brand-RAG + content-analytics (F5.1). The final item: a per-channel brand/style memory (so a channel's generations stay on-brand) + a content-analytics fold (what ships, where pieces sit, the metered cost). Decision: 1. **Per-channel brand memory** (`server/content/brandMemory.ts`) reuses the SINGLE unified RAG store + `retrieve()` under a per-channel sentinel commit `brand:<channelId>` (mirrors the institutional-memory sentinel, ADR 0045). `indexChannelBrand` (re-)indexes a channel's brand snippets; `retrieveChannelBrand` retrieves them for that channel only — no parallel index, no cross-channel leakage. 2. **A PURE content-analytics fold** (`server/content/contentAnalytics.ts` `computeContentAnalytics`) over pieces + media spend + publish jobs → `totalPieces`, `doneCount`, `publishedCount`, `byStage`, `byFormat`, `totalCostCents`, `costByFeature`. Deterministic → testable; views/CTR are placeholders until platform keys land.

chunks.title: Depth program — real gen/render/publish + UI + platform hardening
chunks.text: ADR 0072: Depth program — real gen/render/publish + UI + platform hardening. A 3-agent depth audit (`src/workspaces/_docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md`) found: the code/dev-orchestration side + the contract spine are genuinely deep + real, but (a) the content platform is a hollow stub skeleton — no real generation/render/publish code (the live `generate()` returns `notImplemented`) and NO user-facing UI at all (unreachable; the `snapshot.content` is dead state), and (b) three cross-cutting depth risks: a tenant-isolation leak surface (new + content models are outside `tenantDb`'s loud-fail guarantee), encryption that fails OPEN (`secretBox` → `plain:` when `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` is unset), and ~0% real-infra test coverage. The user wants a real, usable product, not a half-fake one. Decision: Run a `DEPTH_PROGRAM.md` `/goal` build (16 items, H→C→M→U→D) that: 1. **Hardens the platform first** — fold every `workspaceId` model into the tenant isolation guarantee (or lint it) so it can never leak; hard-force `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` (fail-closed). 2. **Fixes the code-side edges** — MR merge/rollback push-to-origin, container readiness probes (no fire-and-forget), retry/backoff + pagination, a real CI-YAML parser + PTY prompt-ready detection. (Docker-dependency is ACCEPTED — no fix.) 3. **Writes the REAL content code behind every `available()` gate** — real Fal/Replicate + ElevenLabs + Suno + Gemini generation, a real ffmpeg (Docker) render pipeline, real YouTube/TikTok OAuth + upload. The stub becom

chunks.title: Tenant-isolation guard via an ai:lint rule (not a full tenantDb fold)
chunks.text: ADR 0073: Tenant-isolation guard via an ai:lint rule (not a full tenantDb fold). `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` cross-cutting #1: `tenantDb`'s loud-fail row-isolation covers only the ~24 core `TENANT_MODELS`. Every newer model (Service/Forge/Environment/CI/Deploy + the ENTIRE content set — 55 models carry `workspaceId`) lives OUTSIDE that guarantee and relies on hand-written `workspaceId` filters on a plain `prisma` client. One forgotten filter = a silent cross-tenant leak; one already existed (`environment.findMany({ status:'live' })`, unscoped). `DEPTH_PROGRAM.md` H1 offered two branches: (a) fold every `workspaceId` model into `tenantDb`'s `TENANT_MODELS`, OR (b) an `ai:lint` rule that forbids a plain-`prisma` read/write on a `workspaceId` model. Decision: Chose branch (b) — a new diff-scoped `tenant-scope` `ai:lint` rule — plus fixing the one known unscoped call. - **The rule:** in `server/**` code, a `prisma.<model>.<read|write>(…)` on any of the 55 `workspaceId`-carrying models that does NOT constrain by `workspaceId` on the call line is a finding. `tenantDb.*` is exempt (it keys off the literal `prisma.` receiver). A deliberate cross-tenant sweep documents itself with `// luckystack-allow tenant-scope: <why>`. - **The known leak:** `reassertEnvironmentRoutes`'s `environment.findMany` is a leader-gated boot self-heal that MUST see every workspace's live envs — marked with the allow-comment (it is a correct cross-tenant sweep, not a leak). - **Verify:** six selftest cases (`npm run a

chunks.title: Secret encryption is fail-closed — WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY is mandatory
chunks.text: ADR 0074: Secret encryption is fail-closed — WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY is mandatory. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` cross-cutting #2: `secretBox` silently fell back to storing `plain:<base64>` (UNENCRYPTED) when `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` was unset, with only a one-time console warning. A `plain:` credential in production is unacceptable — the per-workspace GitLab/GitHub token, DB-connection URLs, and the editor profile blob would land at rest as recoverable plaintext. Decision: Make at-rest encryption **fail-closed**: - `encryptSecret` and `encryptBuffer` now **THROW** a clear error when no key is configured — they never emit a `plain:`/`0x00` plaintext envelope again. - New `assertEncryptionConfigured()` is called at **boot** (in `server.ts`, right after the secret-manager resolves) so the server refuses to start into a state where a stored secret would be plaintext — a loud fatal, not a lazy surprise. - `encryptionConfigured()` is exported for precondition checks. - **Migration path preserved:** `decryptSecret`/`decryptBuffer` STILL read any LEGACY `plain:`/`0x00` values written before this change, so pre-hardening dev data stays readable (re-save such secrets to encrypt them at rest). This closes the fail-OPEN *write* — the actual gap — without silently losing existing data. - **Tests:** `tests/unit/secretBox.test.mts` (14/14) asserts round-trip with a key, tamper→null, encrypt/assert THROW without a key, never-plain:, and legacy decrypt. The test harness (`tests/_helpers.mts`) sets a deterministi

chunks.title: Server-side merge/rollback pushes the target to origin
chunks.text: ADR 0075: Server-side merge/rollback pushes the target to origin. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #1: `mergeBranches`/`revertMergeCommit` advance the `target` branch IN THE LOCAL BARE CLONE, but nothing pushed the result to origin — `pushBranch` existed yet was never called on the merge/rollback path. So a "merged" MR never actually reached the forge ref. Decision: - New `pushRef(workspaceId, gitUrl, token, ref)` in `repoStore` pushes a branch straight from the BARE clone to origin (the merge/revert advance `target` there). Token injected transiently via `withAuth`, never stored/logged. Bounded **retry/backoff** via a new shared `withRetry` helper (`server/util/retry.ts`, reused by C3). - New `pushMergedTarget(prisma, workspaceId, ticketId, targetBranch)` in `forge.ts` resolves the ticket's `project.gitUrl` + the per-project forge token (`resolveForge`) and pushes the target. **Non-fatal:** the local merge is authoritative; a `local-only` project (no gitUrl/token) is a SKIP, and a push failure is surfaced (`pushError`), never rolled back. - Wired into `mergeMr` (after a successful merge) and `rollbackMr` (after a successful revert); `MergeMrResult` gains `pushed?`/`pushError?` so the client/log can see whether the forge received it.

chunks.title: Preview/editor serve paths wait for readiness (no fire-and-forget)
chunks.text: ADR 0076: Preview/editor serve paths wait for readiness (no fire-and-forget). `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #3: the preview + editor flows dispatch a serve-command with `docker exec -d` (detached) and immediately flip the reverse-proxy route + return a URL — assuming success. A real `health.waitForContainerReady` probe existed but was only called by the deploy path (`environment.ts`). So a user opening a preview/editor got a URL that 502s until the dev-server / openvscode-server finished booting (10–30s). Decision: - Parametrized `waitForContainerReady(containerName, port, opts)` — `opts` = `{ attempts, delayMs, acceptAnyStatus, run }`. `acceptAnyStatus` drops curl's `-f` so a token-gated `401` (openvscode's root before the connection-token) still counts as bound; `run` is an injectable probe runner so the retry loop is unit-testable without Docker. - `openPreviewForTicket` now probes `PREVIEW_PORT` after starting the dev server and returns `preview.notReady` on timeout INSTEAD of flipping the route to a dead URL. - `openEditorForTicket` now probes `EDITOR_IN_CONTAINER_PORT` (with `acceptAnyStatus`) after `startEditorInContainer` and returns `editor.notReady` on timeout before flipping the route. - The deploy path (`environment.ts`) already called the probe — unchanged (the new default `opts` is backward-compatible).

chunks.title: Forge issue-sync paginates + retries; git push retries
chunks.text: ADR 0077: Forge issue-sync paginates + retries; git push retries. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #4: `fetchGitlabIssues`/`fetchGithubIssues` fetched a single `per_page=100` page — a project with >100 open issues silently lost the rest. Network ops had no retry/backoff (a transient blip dropped a git push or a sync). Decision: - **Pagination:** a pure `accumulatePages(fetchPage, {perPage, maxPages})` follows `page=1..` until a short page or a safety cap (`MAX_ISSUE_PAGES=20` → 2000 issues). Hitting the cap sets `capped` and the caller `console.warn`s it — **never a silent truncation**. Both GitLab + GitHub sync use it. - **Retry:** each page fetch + `pushBranch` (push-on-approval) run through `withRetry` (ADR 0075). `isTransientForgeError` retries only 5xx/429/network — a 4xx (bad token / not-found) fails fast. - Both helpers exported for a network-free unit test.

chunks.title: Real CI YAML parse + PTY prompt-ready detection
chunks.text: ADR 0078: Real CI YAML parse + PTY prompt-ready detection. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #5: (a) the CI parser was a fixed-indent mini-subset (2-space job names, 4-space fields, inline arrays only) — a real `.gitlab-ci.yml` (top-level jobs, `stages:`/`script:` as block sequences) was largely dropped; (b) the interactive `claude` turn used hardcoded `wait(7000)`/`wait(3000)` before confirming folder-trust + sending the kickoff — fragile on a slow boot, wasteful on a fast one. Decision: - **Real YAML:** a dep-free recursive YAML-subset parser (`parseYamlSubset`) handles block mappings at any consistent indent, block sequences (`- item`), inline flow arrays, quoted scalars, and comments. `parseCiYaml` reads it into the same `CiSpec`, accepting BOTH the documented `jobs:`-wrapped shape (backward compatible) AND a real `.gitlab-ci.yml` (top-level jobs, reserved keys like `variables:` skipped, snake_case `allow_failure`). Still no js-yaml (a transitive dep is a boot-crash risk) and still pure + total (a bad config → `{ok:false}`, never throws). - **PTY prompt-ready:** `server/orchestrator/ptyReady.ts` scans the accumulated PTY output for the CLI's trust/ready markers; `waitForOutput` early-exits as soon as one appears, with a ceiling so a wrong/missing marker DEGRADES to a bounded wait (never a hang, never worse than the old fixed wait). `stageRunner` accumulates `term.onData` and gates the trust-confirm + kickoff on detection.

chunks.title: Real Fal.ai media generation behind available() (stub = no-key fallback)
chunks.text: ADR 0079: Real Fal.ai media generation behind available() (stub = no-key fallback). `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #2: the Fal provider's `generate()` returned `media.notImplemented` — the whole image/video/3d/reference-image surface was fake `stub://`. The user clarified: fake CODE was never asked for (only fake TESTS for the no-key rounds). This item writes the REAL fal.ai code behind `available()`, keeping the stub as the pure no-key fallback. Decision: - `server/media/providers/fal.ts` now has a LIVE `generate()`: it composes the prompt (style system-prompt + prompt + extra instructions, ADR 0053), builds the fal model + input (reference-image/model-3d carry the reference as `image_url`), runs a real fal.ai **queue** request (submit → poll status → fetch result, with retry/backoff), and extracts the produced asset URL per model shape (`images[]`/`video`/`model_mesh`) + a metered € cost. - The HTTP transport is an injectable `FalTransport` so `generate` + the pure helpers (`composeFalInput`/`extractFalAsset`/`liveMediaCostCents`) are unit-tested with FIXTURES — no key, no network. The real transport (`realFalTransport`) is used by default. - `available()` still gates on `FAL_KEY`: no key → the registry never calls `generate` and returns the valid-shaped stub, so the dummy-data pipeline stays green.

chunks.title: Real ElevenLabs voice/sfx + Suno music behind available()
chunks.text: ADR 0080: Real ElevenLabs voice/sfx + Suno music behind available(). `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #2: the ElevenLabs `generate()` returned `media.notImplemented` and music had no real provider. This item writes the REAL code (mirroring M1's fal pattern) behind `available()`. Decision: - **ElevenLabs (voice + sfx):** live `generate()` composes the input (text = style + prompt + extra; voice id from params/env), calls the ElevenLabs REST API (tts → `/text-to-speech/<voice>`, sfx → `/sound-generation`) which returns raw audio BYTES, and persists them via a new `server/media/store.ts` (`data/media/<uuid>.mp3` → a served `/media/...` url). Transport injectable → fixture-tested. - **Suno (music):** a NEW dedicated provider (`server/media/providers/suno.ts`) — `MediaProviderId` gains `'suno'`, registered in the registry, and `music` in the assignments now defaults to `'suno'`. Suno returns a HOSTED audio URL (submit → poll → url), so no local persistence.
