Optional audio is the last input, mapped + `-shortest`. - **`renderScenes(...)`** — the real-video render entry (mirrors `renderTimeline`): localizes each scene's clip/still + the voice, builds the stitch plan, runs the SAME injectable ffmpeg-in-Docker runner, typed degrade on failure. - **`assembly.ts` prefers scenes.** When the piece has a `VideoScene` timeline it renders THAT (real stitch); otherwise it falls back to the beat slideshow. The render metadata (`totalMs`, `sceneCount`) reflects whichever path ran.

chunks.title: V3 — long-video decomposition (content-decompose-video)
chunks.text: ADR 0148: V3 — long-video decomposition (content-decompose-video). The user's flagship ask: "make a 60s video about X" should split into several shorter scenes that FLOW into each other, then stitch. V1 gave the scene model, V2 the stitch. V3 is the step that turns a piece's storyboard (script beats) into a generated, continuity-linked set of scenes. Decision: - **`buildContinuityPrompts(beats)`** (pure, tested): one prompt per beat, where every scene after the first is told to "continue seamlessly from the previous scene: <prev visual>", so consecutive clips are visually coherent. The first scene has no continuity hint; a beat with no `visualPrompt` falls back to its text. - **`decomposeIntoScenes(...)`** generates a clip per beat via the shared queue-aware media lifecycle (`runQueuedMediaAsset`, feature `video-gen` — a stub clip without a key), and creates a `VideoScene` linking it. Scenes after the first crossfade in (`transitionIn: 'xfade'`) so they flow together. Budget-guarded (partial on cap) and re-decomposing REPLACES the scene list. - **`content-decompose-video`** control-op (contentControl route, RBAC work-tickets): finds the piece's latest script and decomposes it; an optional `sceneDurationMs` sets the per-scene length.

chunks.title: V4 — range-refine (content-refine-range)
chunks.text: ADR 0149: V4 — range-refine (content-refine-range). The user's editing vision: "select seconds 13–18 and say refine the transition / voice-over" — iterate a long video without redoing the whole thing. V1–V3 built the scene timeline, stitch, and decomposition; V4 is the targeted edit. Decision: - **`scenesInRange(scenes, startMs, endMs)`** (pure, tested): maps the ordered scenes onto a cumulative timeline and returns those whose interval overlaps the selected range (half-open `[start,end)`), each with its computed `startMs`/`endMs`. - **`refineSceneRange(...)`** regenerates every covered scene as a NEW version: a fresh `video-gen` clip with the instruction folded into the scene's prompt (`<prompt>. Refinement: <instruction>`), a new `VideoScene` with `parentId` = the old scene (I2 lineage) keeping the same order/duration/transition, then the old scene is removed — so the timeline keeps its shape and the edit is traceable. - **`content-refine-range`** control-op (contentControl route, RBAC work-tickets): `{ startMs, endMs, instruction }`; a range that hits no scene is a no-op.

chunks.title: D1 — the real YouTube byte-upload (resumable, all three legs)
chunks.text: ADR 0150: D1 — the real YouTube byte-upload (resumable, all three legs). The audit's sharpest finding: a real YouTube publish never worked, even WITH OAuth keys. `realUploadTransport` did only the resumable INIT (a POST that returns the session URI in its `Location` header + an empty body), then read a video `id` from that empty body — always empty → null → the honesty-fixed publish (ADR 0144) recorded it as an `error`/stub. The actual video bytes were never sent. IDEA_TO_OUTCOME D1 closes that gap so a user with a real Google OAuth app can actually post a video. Decision: - **All three legs of the resumable upload.** `youtubeResumableUpload`: (1) POST the metadata (the existing `buildUploadRequest` init, which carries `X-Upload-Content-Type` so YouTube returns a session URI) and read the `Location` header; (2) read the video bytes; (3) PUT the bytes to the session URI and read the video `id` from the response. Any leg failing → null → the publish is an honest error (never a fake success). - **`buildResumablePut(sessionUri, accessToken)`** — a pure, exported builder for leg 3 (the transport attaches the byte body), unit-tested alongside the init builder. - **`readAssetBytes(assetUrl)`** — reads a local `/media/<file>` from the media store or fetches an http(s) URL; a `stub://`/unknown url yields null (not uploadable). So a real rendered mp4 in the media store uploads directly, without needing a public URL. - **TikTok stays a single init** (PULL_FROM_URL); its status-polling +

chunks.title: D2 — TikTok async publish (status polling)
chunks.text: ADR 0151: D2 — TikTok async publish (status polling). The audit found the TikTok publish fabricated a url: it did the `PULL_FROM_URL` init, got a `publish_id`, and returned `tiktok.com/@me/video/<publish_id>` with NO confirmation — but a `publish_id` is a job id, not a post id, and TikTok publishes asynchronously (the post only exists once the status endpoint reports complete). Decision: - **Poll the status endpoint until confirmed.** `tiktokUpload`: init → `publish_id` → poll `/post/publish/status/fetch/` (bounded, `TIKTOK_POLL_ATTEMPTS`) until `PUBLISH_COMPLETE`, then build the url from the CONFIRMED public post id. `FAILED` or not-confirmed-within-the-window → null (an honest error, per ADR 0144) — never a fabricated url. - **Pure builders/parser:** `buildTiktokStatusRequest(publishId, accessToken)` and `parseTiktokStatus(json)` (status enum + the public post id), unit-tested. The `sleep` between polls is injected so the live poll waits without affecting tests (which inject the whole transport).

chunks.title: O-C — content pipeline orchestration (content-run-pipeline)
chunks.text: ADR 0152: O-C — content pipeline orchestration (content-run-pipeline). Even after V1–V4 (real video) the content side was still "a wall of manual generate buttons" — the user had to fire script, then voice, then images/decompose, then assemble, one at a time. The "idea → outcome" promise needs a single run that turns a brief into a complete piece. O-A lets the Assistant CREATE a content piece; O-C makes it actually PRODUCE the video. Decision: - **`runContentPipeline(...)`** chains the existing step functions — `generateScript` → `generateVoiceover` → (`decomposeIntoScenes` for `mode:'video'` | `generateBeatImages` for `mode:'slideshow'`) → `assembleContent` — into one run. It reuses an existing script rather than regenerating (idempotent-ish), threads the real `scriptId`, and returns which steps ran + whether any output stubbed. NO new generation logic — it composes the reviewed step functions. - **`content-run-pipeline`** control-op (contentControl route, RBAC work-tickets): `{ contentProjectId, mode? }`; `video` is the default (the marquee stitched-scene path). - The run itself is the user's consent (B-23); per-step autonomy-gating (pause for approval between stages, reusing the autonomy dial) is a logged follow-up.

chunks.title: V5/V6 — the video timeline editor UI
chunks.text: ADR 0153: V5/V6 — the video timeline editor UI. V1–V4 built the whole backend of an editable multi-scene video (scene model, stitch render, decomposition, range-refine) but the only way to drive it was raw control-ops. V5 is the editor a user actually operates; V6 (split/delete/transition) folds into it because those are just edits to the scene list the editor saves. Decision: - **`VideoTimelineEditor`** (modal from the content piece page): renders the piece's `VideoScene`s as proportional blocks and drives the existing ops — edit a scene's **duration (trim)** + **transition** (Dropdown), **split** (halve a scene → a new second half), **delete**, **reorder** (left/right) → all saved as the full ordered list via `content-save-scenes` (upsert by id, so ids/lineage survive). A **range selector** (start/end seconds + instruction) fires `content-refine-range`; a **"Generate scenes"** button fires `content-decompose-video`. Every write goes through `runContentOp` → the Conductor (B-23). - **`runContentOp` payload widened to `Record<string, unknown>`** so the editor can pass the scene array + numeric start/end (not just strings); the route validates each op's real shape server-side. - **Reorder/split/trim are buttons + inputs, not raw drag.** They are reliable, keyboard-accessible, and produce exactly the same scene-list save; drag is a logged follow-up (it needs live browser tuning).

chunks.title: O-D — "start with AI" auto-activation
chunks.text: ADR 0154: O-D — "start with AI" auto-activation. To start the AI on a new ticket the user had to create it (lands at `unrefined`, AI off) and then MANUALLY drag it into the first AI stage. IDEA_TO_OUTCOME O-D removes that step for the common "I want the AI on this now" case. Decision: - **`quick-add` gains an optional `startWithAi` flag.** The ticket still ENTERS at `unrefined` (the invariant "a user-created ticket always enters at unrefined; no client can place it mid-pipeline" is preserved — the Conductor is the writer). Then, when `startWithAi` is set, the Conductor advances it to the FIRST `aiEnabled` stage, records a `status-change` event ("auto-started AI at <stage>"), and runs `activateWorktreesForStage` (a no-op without a linked repo/Docker, as usual). It returns the ADVANCED row so the realtime delta shows the new stage. - **Wired end to end:** the `workspaces/quickAdd` route threads `startWithAi`; the client `quickAdd` helper + the New-ticket form expose a checkbox ("Start with AI right away", i18n ×4).

chunks.title: B1 — client-side crop + resize in the image editor
chunks.text: ADR 0155: B1 — client-side crop + resize in the image editor. The image editor already did adjustments (B/C/S), one-tap looks (B3), and a text overlay (B2), all as non-destructive Fabric-canvas edits exported to a NEW asset via the tested `content-import-asset` flow. B1 adds the two remaining "essentials" the program calls for — crop and resize-to-preset — without leaving that client-side, no-provider model. Decision: - **Crop is a draggable/resizable Fabric `Rect`** toggled on: its `getBoundingRect()` (clamped to the canvas by the pure `clampCropRegion`) becomes the exported sub-region via Fabric's `toDataURL({left,top,width,height})`. The rect is removed before export so it isn't baked into the output. - **Resize is a preset dropdown** (`Original / 1080 / 720 / 512` px width) applied after crop through an offscreen 2D-canvas draw sized by the pure `resizeDimensions` (shrink-only, aspect-preserving). - **The geometry lives in a Fabric-free helper** (`_functions/imageCrop.ts`) so `clampCropRegion` (clamp, invert-normalise, degenerate→null) and `resizeDimensions` are unit-tested without a canvas (11/11). - **No new op, no provider, no spend.** Export still goes through the existing upload + `content-import-asset` path (B-23: the Conductor writes the asset), identical to B2/B3.

chunks.title: P-B — structured approve/reject/choice cards for needs-input
chunks.text: ADR 0156: P-B — structured approve/reject/choice cards for needs-input. When an in-container agent blocked on a question it emitted a `ws-needs-input` block. Two problems: (1) the parsed questions were **dropped** — `stageRunner` parked the session busy but never wrote the question onto the ticket, so the human saw nothing; (2) even the defer-message banner was a single free-text input, so a yes/no or pick-one decision meant typing prose on a phone. P-B makes the agent's question actually surface, and as a structured, tap-to-answer card. Decision: - **Encode structure inside the existing `needsInput` string — no schema change, no new verb.** A FREE question stays its plain prompt (every existing reader — banner, answer-queue, `isRealNeedsInput` — is unaffected); an APPROVE or CHOICE question is stored as a compact `@@wsq:` JSON envelope. The pure, isomorphic `structuredQuestion.ts` (`encodeQuestion` / `parseStructuredQuestion` / `questionPrompt`) is the single wire-shape source shared by server and client. - **Close the surfacing gap in `stageRunner`.** On a needs-input turn, persist the first question (already needsInput-encoded by `parseTurnResult`) onto the ticket + flip it to `needs-input` + broadcast, so the board/phone renders the card. `parseTurnResult` now accepts structured entries (`{prompt,kind,options}`) alongside bare strings. - **The card (`NeedsInputBanner`) renders by kind:** approve → Approve/Reject (+ optional note); choice → one tap-target per option; free

chunks.title: D4 — prod build-export (bundle) + external deploy-hook
chunks.text: ADR 0157: D4 — prod build-export (bundle) + external deploy-hook. `build-export` produced only a `docker save` image tarball; the `bundle` kind (a real production build, `npm run build` → dist/) returned `export.bundleNotImplemented`. And there was no way to hand a built artifact to an external server — the "prod = CI/CD to another host" half of the idea→outcome vision. D4 implements both, on the existing Docker + BuildArtifact + signed-download plumbing (no new op — `build-export` already exists and is RBAC-gated). Decision: - **Bundle export runs the REAL build inside a throwaway container from the project image**: `docker run` `<buildCmd> && tar -czf /tmp/bundle.tgz -C <outputDir> .`, then `docker cp` the single tarball out, then `docker rm -f`. Build + tar happen IN the container (the app image has node + tar/gzip), so nothing is assumed about the host — it works cross-platform (the host never tars). `buildCmd`/`outputDir` are read from env at CALL time (`WS_BUILD_EXPORT_CMD` default `cd /app && npm run build`, `WS_BUILD_EXPORT_DIR` default `/app/dist`) so a non-standard project pins its own build without a code change or restart. - **The deploy-hook is a webhook POST** of a self-describing descriptor (`event, workspaceId, projectId, kind, artifactId, imageRef, downloadToken`) to `WS_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL` (+ optional bearer), fired automatically after a ready artifact. The fetch is injectable (`DeployFetch`) so it is E2E-tested against a real local HTTP receiver. Unconfigur

chunks.title: D3 — demo-host (main on a DNS) + auto-redeploy watcher
chunks.text: ADR 0158: D3 — demo-host (main on a DNS) + auto-redeploy watcher. The deploy engine already runs a project's target branch (main) at a stable route (`<kind>-<slug>.<domain>`) via Caddy + Docker. What was missing for "main draait op DNS X" as a demo surface: a dedicated demo kind and the thing that makes a demo useful — it stays current as main advances, or is deliberately frozen at a commit for a stable link. Decision: - **A `demo` env kind** (added to `ENV_KINDS`) that reuses the whole existing deploy path (clone target branch → serve → readiness → flip the stable route). No parallel deploy engine. - **Three fields on `Environment`** (MongoDB — no migration): `deployedCommit` (what the current deploy runs), `autoRedeploy` (follow main), `pinnedCommit` (freeze at a fixed commit; disables auto-redeploy and is `git checkout`'d in the container so the demo serves that exact commit). - **A leader-gated `demoWatch` sweep** (`startDemoWatcher`, same shape as the cron/publish schedulers): every tick it resolves each demo env's target-branch head (`branchHead`) and redeploys when it moved. The decision is the pure `shouldRedeployDemo` (auto on + not pinned + known head + head ≠ deployed); head-resolution and deploy are injectable so the sweep is tested with injected git-state, no git/container needed. - **`ensureEnvironment` defaults a demo to autoRedeploy=true** unless a `pinnedCommit` is given (a pin always wins); `env-deploy` passes `pinnedCommit`/`autoRedeploy` through. No new op

chunks.title: G1 — greenfield: real repo + seed file-tree generation
chunks.text: ADR 0159: G1 — greenfield: real repo + seed file-tree generation. `project-from-template` created a Project row + seeded convention docs + a default pipeline, but never made a REPO — `gitlabPath:''`, no `gitUrl`, no bare clone. So `isLinked` stayed false, the runtime couldn't cut a worktree, and no container/code followed. A "greenfield" project was a shell with nothing to edit. G1 makes it a real, runnable starting point with no external forge. Decision: - **Templates carry a seed `files` tree** (`StarterFile[]`) — a minimal but runnable skeleton per stack (package.json + entry + config + README + .gitignore for node-api / react-vite; requirements.txt + app/main .py for fastapi). Not a full app: the starting point the impl-stage agent fleshes out. - **`initGreenfieldRepo(workspaceId, files)` in repoStore** writes the tree into a temp checkout, `git init -b main` + a self-contained identity + commit, then `git clone --bare` into the durable per-workspace `repo.git`. `isLinked` flips true → the existing worktree/container path just works (container → code). It is a **no-op when a repo already exists** (never clobber a linked repo), and self-contained (no external forge, no network). - **`project-from-template` calls it best-effort** and stamps the project `gitUrl: greenfield://<workspaceId>` when it linked, so the UI/status treats it as a linked project. A git failure logs + leaves the project unlinked (the row + pipeline still exist).

chunks.title: G2 — greenfield template-wizard UI
chunks.text: ADR 0160: G2 — greenfield template-wizard UI. G1 made `project-from-template` produce a real repo, and both `createFromTemplate` (provider) and the `templates` catalog (snapshot) were already exposed — but nothing in the UI rendered them, so a user could never pick a stack template. G2 is the front door onto the greenfield op. Decision: - **Extend the existing `CreateProjectForm`** (the "New project" menu off the project switcher) with a two-mode toggle: **From a template** (greenfield — a stack-template picker → `createFromTemplate`, which runs G1's real-repo init) and **Link a repo** (the pre-existing name + git-URL → `createProject`). Template mode is the default (greenfield-first). - **The picker is driven by the snapshot `templates`** (label + description cards, single-select). Submit branches on mode; the create button disables until a name (and, in template mode, a template) is chosen. - **No new op, no new screen file.** The wizard is the create-project menu the switcher already opens, so it works for the first project and every later one.

chunks.title: V5 completion — the timeline audio track (waveform + voice/duck sliders)
chunks.text: ADR 0161: V5 completion — the timeline audio track (waveform + voice/duck sliders). V5's timeline editor shipped scenes + trim + transitions + range-refine, but the spec's last piece — "een audio-spoor met de E4-waveform + volume/duck-sliders" — was missing, and the render only ever mixed the voiceover (music + per-track gains were unreachable). This closes that gap so a user can see and balance the audio and have it actually affect the rendered video. Decision: - **Per-piece mix on `ContentProject`** (MongoDB, no migration): `voiceVolume` (default 1) + `musicVolume` (default 0.25, ducked). Persisted by a new **`content-save-audio-mix`** control-op (content-* write family; no new frozen verb) — RBAC `workTickets`, clamped (voice ≤ 2, music ≤ 1) by the Conductor (B-23). - **The render honours the gains.** `buildVideoStitchPlan` gained an optional `mix` ({musicFile, voiceVolume, musicVolume}); when there's music OR a non-default voice gain it routes voice (+ ducked music) through the existing `buildAudioMixPlan` (E4) → `[aout]`. **Guarded** so the plain single-voice path is byte-identical — the live render test is unchanged (re-run 7/7). `renderScenes` + `assembly` thread the piece's music asset + gains in. - **The snapshot surfaces** `voiceVolume`/`musicVolume` + the newest voice/music asset urls on `ContentPieceSummary`, so the editor can draw the track without another fetch. - **A real waveform** in `VideoTimelineEditor`: `decodePeaks` fetches + `decodeAudioData` → per-block

chunks.title: W1 — multi-question sets via denormalized JSON on the ticket (not the relational QuestionSet models)
chunks.text: ADR 0162: W1 — multi-question sets via denormalized JSON on the ticket (not the relational QuestionSet models). An in-container agent can end its turn with a `ws-needs-input` block listing **several** questions (`parseTurnResult` already returns `questions: string[]`), but `stageRunner` persisted only `questions[0]` onto the single `Ticket.needsInput` banner and **silently dropped the rest**. So a phone-first "answer a few questions" flow was impossible — if the agent asked 3, 2 were lost. The schema already modelled relational `QuestionSet` + `Question` tables (04b, "phone-from-the-beach loop") but they were **dead code** — nothing read or wrote them, and the docs (02 §2/§5, features/09) described a **blocking `request_input` held-open verb** that was never implemented (the real mechanism is park-and-resume via the Stop-hook). W1 makes multi-question real and the docs honest. Decision: - **Store the full set denormalized on the ticket**, not in the relational models: add `Ticket.needsInputQuestions Json?` = `[{ q, a }]` (q = the stored needsInput wire form — plain for free, `@@wsq:` for approve/choice; a = the answer or null). `Ticket.needsInput` stays the banner = the first UNANSWERED question (back-compat with every existing reader: the banner, the answer-queue, `isRealNeedsInput`, the P-B card). - **A pure core module** `server/orchestrator/questionSet.ts` (`parseNeedsInputQuestions` with a legacy single-banner fallback, `applyAnswers`, `firstUnanswered`, `buildCombinedAn

chunks.title: W2 — non-blocking (advisory) questions via the done-envelope, resolved with a divergence→revision loop
chunks.text: ADR 0163: W2 — non-blocking (advisory) questions via the done-envelope, resolved with a divergence→revision loop. The user wants the agent to be able to ASK a question without fully blocking the ticket — "de AI kan vragen stellen maar wel al verder met de rest" (mostly code-side). In the park-and-resume model a `ws-needs-input` block STOPS the turn (parks the ticket), which is the opposite of "keep working". So a non-blocking question cannot travel through `ws-needs-input`; it must be something the agent notes *while proceeding*. The plan's phrasing ("re-express via de bestaande needs-input-payload + answer-input") was ambiguous about the exact mechanism, so per the run's ambiguity rule this design was chosen and logged as an OPEN VRAAG in the branch-log. Decision: - **A non-blocking question rides the DONE envelope, not `ws-needs-input`.** The agent, instead of stopping, makes a sensible assumption, keeps working, and records the question in the `ws-carryover` block's `openQuestions` as an object `{ question, assumption }`. `parseTurnResult` splits `openQuestions` into plain strings (unchanged, still fed to the next stage's `{{openQuestions}}` as before) + `advisories` (`{q, assumption}`). renderStage's guidance now tells the agent this explicitly, reserving `ws-needs-input` for TRULY blocking questions. - **The ticket never parks on an advisory.** On stage-done, advisories are appended (dedup by question) to a new denormalized `Ticket.advisoryQuestions Json?` = `[{q,assumpt

chunks.title: T1 — preview an arbitrary git ref via an ephemeral, ref-scoped container (un-defer preview-at-ref)
chunks.text: ADR 0164: T1 — preview an arbitrary git ref via an ephemeral, ref-scoped container (un-defer preview-at-ref). Every run/preview/deploy path was hardwired to the branch TIP: `launchTicketContainer` clones `git clone --branch <branch> --single-branch`, `openPreview` took only `{workspaceId, ticketKey}`, and previewing a specific/older commit was explicitly "Deferred" (`features/23_PREVIEW_DEPLOYMENT.md`). The user wants "start a server from main but without commit X" / "run yesterday's version" (T2 builds the synthetic-ref producer on top of this) — which requires previewing an arbitrary ref. Decision: - **A ref-preview runs in its OWN ephemeral, ref-scoped container** — NOT the ticket's tip worker container. `launchTicketContainer` gains an optional `ref`: when present, the container/volume name get a `-ref-<slug>` suffix (`refSlug`, ≤12 docker-safe chars) and the clone becomes a FULL-history `git clone /mirror /work` + `git checkout <ref>` (`cloneExecArgs`, pure + tested) instead of the single-branch tip clone. So two refs of one branch coexist and a ref-preview never clobbers the agent's tip working container. - **Ref-scoped route** (`refPreviewRoute`): distinct `id` (`<ticketKey>-ref-<slug>`) + subdomain (`<branch>-<slug>.<domain>`) per ref → side-by-side previews, idempotent per ref. - **Injection-safe ref**: `isSafeRef` gates on `[0-9a-zA-Z._/-]` with no `..` before the ref reaches the clone shell; `openRefPreview` (+ the `open-ref-preview_v1` `_api` op, `workTickets`-gat

chunks.title: S1 — any-stack via a multi-base catalog sharing one agent base (relaxed Dockerfile-trust guard)
chunks.text: ADR 0165: S1 — any-stack via a multi-base catalog sharing one agent base (relaxed Dockerfile-trust guard). Every project image was forced to `FROM workspaces/base` (Node), enforced by THREE triplicated `extendsBase` guards; Python/Go/Rust were only reachable as an Admin-gated, linked-repo-only AI-generated Dockerfile that `apt`-layered a toolchain onto the full Node base, and the one non-Node template couldn't actually run. The user wants to build on ANY stack. The audit called this the #3 dev blocker. Decision: - **One agent base, N stack variants.** The coding agent (`claude` CLI), `node-pty`, openvscode-server, the pty-agent, and the DB/git tooling are Node-based and MUST run in EVERY container — so a "clean per-stack image" is impossible; instead each stack base (`docker/base-<stack>.Dockerfile`) does `FROM workspaces/base` and adds ONLY that stack's toolchain (python/go/rust/jdk). The user's app builds/runs in the stack; the agent runs on the inherited Node layer. - **A first-class catalog** (`server/container/baseImages.ts`): `BASE_STACKS = node|python|go|rust|java`, `baseImageFor(stack)` (node = the agent base, others = `workspaces/base-<stack>`, env-overridable), `resolveProjectBaseImage(project)` = the built L2 `baseImageRef` else the stack base. New `Project.stack` field (null = node) selects it; the launch callers (stageRunner, preview, ref-preview) resolve through it. - **The Dockerfile-trust guard is relaxed to the FAMILY** (`extendsAllowedBase`): the first `FROM

chunks.title: K1 — third-party services via a sanitized, per-workspace-namespaced docker-compose engine
chunks.text: ADR 0166: K1 — third-party services via a sanitized, per-workspace-namespaced docker-compose engine. There was NO way to attach a third-party service (Postgres/Kafka/Redis/Elasticsearch) to a workspace — the "catalog" only stored a connection string + a (missing) MCP script and provisioned nothing. The user wants "run any docker-compose" so ANY tool is reachable, and correctly noted that running the services is just `docker compose up` — the real edges are multi-tenancy + security. Decision: - **A compose-ENGINE, not a fixed catalog.** A workspace attaches an arbitrary docker-compose file (`service-provision` control-op). K2 presets are curated compose snippets on top; the engine is the core. - **Fail-closed SANITIZER (K1-a, `composeSanitize`)** gates every compose before it is stored or run: host-escape directives (`privileged`, `cap_add`, `devices`, `security_opt`, host bind-mounts, `/var/run/docker.sock`, `network_mode|pid|ipc: host`) REJECT the file (structural parse via the dep-free `parseYamlSubset` + a raw-text scan that catches flow-style); published host ports are REWRITTEN to container-only (no cross-workspace port collision — services are reached intra-network by name). - **Per-workspace namespacing (K1-b, `composeEngine`)**: the compose runs under project `ws-<id>-<name>` on an EXTERNAL per-workspace network `ws-<id>-svc` injected into the compose (so the app/preview container + the services share one net); Docker prefixes volumes by project. chunks.title: H1 — an append-only admin/security audit log for governance ops
chunks.text: ADR 0167: H1 — an append-only admin/security audit log for governance ops. The team-readiness audit found the #1 admin-trust blocker: governance ops — `change-role`, `save-env`/ `remove-env`, `remove-member`, `transfer-ownership`, `delete-workspace`, `role-update`, `invite` — mutated authoritative state but left **ZERO** trace (no `AuditLog` model; `recordTicketEvent` needs a ticketId, so non-ticket governance events were invisible). An admin could not answer "who changed this person's role / read this secret / removed this member / transferred ownership, and when." For a self-hosted tool that writes code + holds secrets, that's a hard "no" at many orgs. Decision: - **A dedicated append-only `AuditLog`** (`{workspaceId, actorId, action, target, metadata, createdAt}`), separate from `TicketEvent` (which is per-ticket + seq-ordered). A pure `recordAudit(prisma, ws, actorId, action, target?, meta?)` helper — best-effort (a failure NEVER breaks the op; the authoritative write already ran) — is called at the END of each governance conductor case, on the Conductor (the only writer, B-23). - **Never log the secret VALUE** — `save-env` records the KEY + `{secret: true}`, never the plaintext; the metadata carries only safe context (old→new role, invited email + role). - **A read view** (`listAuditLog` + `audit-log_v1` `_api`, `workspaceSettings`-gated) returns the entries newest-first with the actor's name resolved, tenant-scoped.

chunks.title: H5 — fair (round-robin) capacity draining across workspaces
chunks.text: ADR 0168: H5 — fair (round-robin) capacity draining across workspaces. The CapacityManager (#12, ADR 0019-sibling) parks turns that exceed the host-wide concurrency cap on a single FIFO queue and drains one per slot-release. FIFO is unfair across tenants: a workspace that floods the queue with 20 tickets is served entirely before another workspace's single waiting ticket — one busy tenant starves the rest. The audit flagged this as a multi-tenant fairness gap. Decision: - **Drain the LEAST-LOADED workspace first** (round-robin), FIFO within a workspace. On each slot-release, `drainCapacityQueue` reads current occupancy per workspace and `pickFairNext` selects the earliest-queued turn whose workspace holds the fewest active slots (strict-less-than on ties preserves FIFO). - **Occupancy per workspace is derived from the active set**, made possible by TAGGING each active ZSET member as `<workspaceId>::<ticketKey>` (was the bare ticketKey). This keeps the existing TTL self-healing (the score is still acquire-time, so a crashed instance's slots still evict) — no drift-prone side counter. - **`pickFairNext` is pure** (queue items + an in-flight map → the chosen item + index), unit-tested; the Redis read/LREM lives in `dequeueFairDeferred`.

chunks.title: 0250-product-self-knowledge-corpus
chunks.text: ADR 0250: 0250-product-self-knowledge-corpus. The in-app Workspace-AI grounds only on the workspace snapshot + the user's linked code (RAG). It has ZERO knowledge of what the PRODUCT itself can do, so it cannot answer "can we edit videos?" ("yes — via the media module, first generate/upload a video then use the timeline editor"). The rich self-knowledge (161 ADRs + the capability inventory) exists as committed docs but is only reachable by the dev-time `@luckystack/mcp` server, never at runtime. Q1 compiles that knowledge into a retrievable corpus. > **ADR numbering:** this program (`AI_LIBRARIES_ACCOUNTS_PROGRAM.md`) runs on the `feat/ai-libraries-accounts` > branch in parallel with the ADOPTION run, which consumes 0162+. To avoid merge-time number collisions, this > program's ADRs start at **0250**. Decision: - **A hand-curated capability Q&A** (`docs/product-knowledge/capabilities.md`) is the primary source: plain- language "can I do X? → yes, via module Y, steps ..." blocks, one `### Q:` per capability. This is what makes the AI genuinely helpful ("how do I ...") rather than just factual. - **A deterministic generator** (`scripts/generateProductKnowledge.mjs`, `npm run ai:product-knowledge`, wired into the pre-commit hook) compiles the Q&A + every ADR (title + Context/Decision summary) into two artifacts: `docs/AI_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE.md` (human digest) + `docs/AI_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE.json` (`{hash, chunks:[{id,kind,title,text}]}` — the embedding input). Pure-Node, no timestamp

chunks.title: 0251-product-knowledge-rag-corpus
chunks.text: ADR 0251: 0251-product-knowledge-rag-corpus. Q1 compiled the product's self-knowledge into `docs/AI_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE.json` (capability Q&A + ADR summaries). Q2 makes it retrievable at chat-time so the Workspace-AI can answer capability questions. The RAG store (`RagEntry` + `retrieve()`) already exists and is reused twice for non-code corpora (institutional memory, per-channel brand) via a sentinel "commit" — this is the third instance. Decision: - **`server/rag/productKnowledge.ts`** indexes the compiled corpus into `RagEntry` under a GLOBAL scope: a reserved sentinel `workspaceId` = the zero ObjectId `000000000000000000000000` (no real workspace) + a sentinel `commitHash` = `product-knowledge`. `retrieveProductKnowledge(prisma, query, k)` = `retrieve(..., PRODUCT_WS, ..., PRODUCT_COMMIT)`, excluding a meta/marker row. Reuses the one embedder + the one cosine scan — no parallel retrieval path. - **Idempotent on the corpus hash.** A marker row (`__product_meta__`) records the indexed hash; the boot `ensureProductKnowledge` re-embeds only when the corpus changed. Indexed once at boot, leader-gated + delayed so leadership has settled; best-effort (never blocks/breaks boot). - **Deterministic + offline-testable.** In the default test world the LOCAL embedder (no GEMINI key) is used, so the E2E is deterministic and free: "can I edit videos?" retrieves the media/timeline-editor chunk.

chunks.title: 0252-wire-product-knowledge-into-ai
chunks.text: ADR 0252: 0252-wire-product-knowledge-into-ai. Q1 compiled the product's self-knowledge and Q2 made it retrievable, but nothing consumed it yet. Q3 wires it into the in-app AI so it actually answers "can we edit videos?" from the corpus. Decision: - **`workspaceChat.interpretChat` retrieves the product corpus** (`retrieveProductKnowledge(message, 4)`) alongside the existing code-RAG, and injects it into the system prompt as a SEPARATE "What THIS product can do" section — deliberately distinct from the user-code section so the model never confuses product capabilities with the user's repository. A new instruction tells it to answer whether/how questions from that section (name the module + steps) and, when a first step maps to an op, propose it. - **A compact global capability index in `registry.workspaceAiPrefix`/`runAiCompletion`** — the capability TITLES (not the full corpus), read once from the compiled shard + cached, prepended to EVERY feature's system prompt at the single choke-point. So the whole AI surface is product-aware, cheaply (~15 lines), with the detail retrieved on demand in chat. - **B-23 unchanged.** The assistant still only proposes; the Conductor is the single writer.

chunks.title: 0253-premade-look-gallery
chunks.text: ADR 0253: 0253-premade-look-gallery. The Designer module already had the building blocks — palettes (DesignTheme), component styles (DesignStyle, incl. Apple/Material/Glass/Brutalist), animations, fonts — with live-preview via `themeVars`/`styleVars`. But there was no curated CATALOG of ready-made looks to browse + apply, and no rich preview surfaces (a real landing/menu/animation/font showcase). L1 adds that reference gallery. Decision: - **A premade-look catalog as curated COMBINATIONS of the existing seeds** (`premades.ts`): a "look" pairs a seed palette + a seed style + an animation + heading/body fonts. Eight starter looks (Apple, Material, Glass, Brutalist, Minimal, Editorial, Playful, Neumorphic) — a strong STARTER that upload/copy/customize (L3) extends. Pure data + a `resolveLook` resolver; no new palette authoring. - **A `Gallery` section** (now the Designer's default tab) renders the catalog as thumbnails and, for the selected look, live preview SURFACES under the look's vars: a nav menu, a landing hero, a card row, a replayable entrance animation (motion/react + the seed AnimSpec), and a font showcase. Tailwind colour classes inside the preview read the OVERRIDDEN `--color-*` vars, so the subtree re-themes; `--ds-*` drives the shapes. "Use this look" applies its theme + style via the existing persist path.

chunks.title: 0254-designer-persistence-roundtrip
chunks.text: ADR 0254: 0254-designer-persistence-roundtrip. The Designer's libraries (themes/styles/anims) were client-held `useState` seeded from `SEED_*`. Saving a look wrote a `DesignArtifact` (save + setActive), but nothing loaded them BACK — persistence was one-directional, so a saved theme vanished on reload and never appeared in the gallery/rails. The snapshot already exposes the full `designArtifacts` rows (content included); they were consumed only for the active name. Decision: - **Consume the existing snapshot `designArtifacts` — no new `list`/`load` op.** The snapshot IS the list. `persisted.ts` parses each row back into the typed shape (`artifactToTheme`/`Style`/`Anim` + a `parsePersistedLibraries` splitter), defensively: a malformed/half-set row coerces to null (never crashes the designer). The content shapes match what `useInProject` writes (`{light,dark}` for a theme, the full spec for a style/anim). - **`state.tsx` merges the persisted artifacts into the libraries** via a `useEffect` on `designArtifacts`, appending by id (idempotent), never clobbering unsaved local edits. So a saved look reappears on reload AND live right after saving (refetch → the effect re-runs).

chunks.title: 0255-designer-import-copy-crud
chunks.text: ADR 0255: 0255-designer-import-copy-crud. L1 gave a premade-look gallery and L2 the persistence round-trip. L3 lets a user make the library their own: copy a premade into their workspace, import a theme/style JSON, customize it, and delete their own. Decision: - **Copy a premade → workspace artifacts.** `lookToArtifacts(resolved)` produces a theme artifact (its palette) + a style artifact (its component spec with the look's fonts baked in), saved via the existing `designerLibrary` `save` op. They round-trip (L2) into the editable rails, so "copy" = "make it mine". - **Import a theme/style/anim JSON.** A file picker in the gallery reads the JSON, and **`validArtifactContent` (pure, reuses the L2 coercion) refuses anything that isn't a real theme/style/anim** before saving — a garbage upload can't poison the library. Reuses `save`; no new op. - **Customize + delete reuse existing surfaces.** Rail edits (rename/duplicate/token-edit) now persist through L2; delete is the existing per-workspace `deleteDesignArtifact` (premades/seeds stay read-only).

chunks.title: 0256-style-through-video-path
chunks.text: ADR 0256: 0256-style-through-video-path. Picking a style ("stick-man figures") only affected the SLIDESHOW path (per-beat images all styled). The real-video path was ungenerated-style: `runContentPipeline` did not pass its `opts` to `decomposeIntoScenes`, and `decomposeIntoScenes` had no `styleKey` param — it sent each scene's beat prompt with NO `style`. So a styled video request produced unstyled clips. This is the single highest-value content fix in the program. Decision: - **`decomposeIntoScenes` resolves the piece's `video-gen` style and rides it on every scene request.** It gained `styleKey`/`extraInstructions` params, calls `resolveStyle(ws, 'video-gen', styleKey)`, and passes `request.style` + `styleId` — the exact pattern `images.ts` already uses for the slideshow path. - **`buildSceneRequest` is extracted (pure + exported)** so a unit test asserts the style rides every scene- gen request, deterministically. - **The wiring is completed end-to-end:** `runContentPipeline` now forwards `...opts` to `decomposeIntoScenes`, and the two conductor ops (`content-run-pipeline`, `content-decompose-video`) forward `styleKey` + `extraInstructions` from the payload.

chunks.title: 0257-style-preview-asset
chunks.text: ADR 0257: 0257-style-preview-asset. Media styles were a text-only list (label + systemPrompt) picked from a name dropdown — nothing showed a sample of the LOOK, so a user couldn't say "I like THIS look". `StylePreset.params` already existed; only a preview reference was missing. Decision: - **Two nullable columns on `StylePreset`**: `previewAssetUrl` (a sample image/video of the style) + `previewKind` ('image'|'video') — MongoDB, no migration. Threaded through `listStyles` (ResolvedStyle), the `save-style` op, and the snapshot's `content.styles`, so a style carries its preview end to end. - **The picker shows the chosen style's preview** (a looping muted `

chunks.title: 0258-longform-video-planner
chunks.text: ADR 0258: 0258-longform-video-planner. The pipeline emitted a fixed 4–8 beats → ~20–40s videos; there was no way to ask for a longer video, and "pick a look + topic → make a video" needed the style to reach the video path (M2, done). M3 adds the duration planner so "a 10-minute video about the moon landing in stick-man figures" is expressible. Decision: - **A pure `planBeatCount(targetDurationMs, sceneDurationMs)`** maps a target duration to ~N beats/scenes (each ≈ sceneDuration), bounded to [2, `MAX_BEATS` = 40]. The media budget stays the true hard cap; 40 is the planner ceiling so a runaway target can't fan out to hundreds of paid clips. - **`generateScript` gained `targetBeats`** → `scriptFormat(targetBeats)` asks the model for ~N beats, and the stub script yields exactly N (deterministic in the stub world). `runContentPipeline` gained `durationMs` + `sceneDurationMs`, plans the beat count, threads it to the script + the per-scene length to decompose. The `content-run-pipeline` op forwards both. - **A Length picker** (Auto / Short / Normal / Long) on the piece page sets `durationMs`; combined with the M1 style picker, that IS "pick a look + a length → make a video". 0 = auto (the default arc).

chunks.title: 0259-media-style-crud-roundtrip
chunks.text: ADR 0259: 0259-media-style-crud-roundtrip. M1 gave styles a preview asset + params. The style CRUD (save-style/delete-style) and the portable style-set export/import already existed, but were TEXT-ONLY — a copied/shared style lost its preview. M4 makes the whole CRUD + portability preview-aware. Decision: - **`save-style` + `delete-style` already do create/customize/delete** per-workspace (builtins stay read-only); M1 made `save-style` accept `previewAssetUrl`/`previewKind`. - **The portable style-set carries the preview.** `StyleSetEntry` + `parseStyleSet` + `exportStyleSet` + `importStyleSet` gained `previewAssetUrl`/`previewKind`, so export → parse → import preserves the look. This is the "copy/share a style and keep its look" path. - **Copy a builtin into the workspace = a `save-style` pre-filled** from the gallery/builtin entry (a new key, editable) — reusing the existing op, no new surface.

chunks.title: 0260-multi-account-channel-management
chunks.text: ADR 0260: 0260-multi-account-channel-management. Publishing stored ONE token per platform (`__publish_<platform>`), so connecting a second YouTube account overwrote the first; and channels (a platform + brand identity) could only be created in tests — no create/edit/delete op or UI. A1+A2 make "manage all your social accounts + channels via the workspace" real. Decision: - **A1 — re-key the connection store** so `tokenKey(platform, accountId?)` = `__publish_<platform>` (default, back-compat) or `__publish_<platform>_<accountId>` for N accounts per platform. `saveConnection`/ `getConnection` gained an optional `accountId`. The token-refresh logic (ADOPTION F1) stays orthogonal — this only changes the KEY, not the read/refresh. - **A2 — channel + account management ops** (content-* write family, RBAC): `channel-create`/`channel-edit`/ `channel-delete` (a channel = projectId + name + platform + handle + brandVoice + defaultStyleId) and `account-disconnect` (remove a connected account's token by platform + optional accountId). Channels are already on the snapshot; the CRUD makes them user-managed.

chunks.title: 0261-publish-routing-content-channel
chunks.text: ADR 0261: 0261-publish-routing-content-channel. A1+A2 gave N accounts per platform + channel management. A3 makes a publish target a CHOSEN account (not just "the platform"), and A4 lets a content piece be created bound to a channel ("make a video for channel Z") so generation grounds on that channel's brand. Decision: - **A3 — thread `accountId` through the publish path.** `performUpload` + `publishAsset` gained an optional `accountId` → `getConnection(platform, accountId)`, so the upload uses the chosen account's token (default account when omitted). `content-request-publish` carries `accountId` in the suggestion patch; the accept passes it to `publishAsset`. - **A4 — `content-from-brief` accepts `channelId`.** The created `ContentProject` is bound to the channel (content-create already did), so `brandContext` + brand-RAG ground every generation on that channel's voice. The Workspace-AI can propose "make a video for channel Z" by re-expressing it as a content-create/ content-from-brief with the channelId (no new verb).

chunks.title: 0262-content-best-practices-playbook
chunks.text: ADR 0262: 0262-content-best-practices-playbook. The content AI knew what the PRODUCT can do (product-knowledge corpus) and HOW to render (styles), but not what makes content WORK — hooks, retention structure, thumbnail principles, ad structure, per-platform rules. So a generated script was on-brand but not necessarily good. Domain craft was missing. Decision: - **A curated `docs/content-playbook/playbook.md`** holds platform-agnostic craft knowledge, one retrievable chunk per `###` section (hooks, scripts/retention, thumbnails, per-platform, ads). - **A fourth global RAG corpus** (`server/rag/contentPlaybook.ts`) — same second-corpus pattern as product-knowledge/memory/brand: the ONE embedder + the ONE `retrieve()`, global zero-ObjectId sentinel workspace, distinct commit `content-playbook`, idempotent on a content hash, boot-ensured leader-gated. The markdown is chunked at RUNTIME (no compiled JSON / generator needed — it's small + hand-curated). - **`generateScript` grounds on it**: retrieves the top-3 best-practices relevant to the brief and injects them as a "Proven content best-practices (apply these)" section in the system prompt, alongside brand + knowledge.

chunks.title: 0263-inspiration-reference-library
chunks.text: ADR 0263: 0263-inspiration-reference-library. Styles say HOW output renders and the best-practices playbook says what works in GENERAL, but there was no way for a workspace to say "make it like THESE examples" — the great ads/thumbnails/intros they've collected. That concrete, per-workspace inspiration was missing. Decision: - **A `ReferenceExample` model** (kind, title, `description` = why it works, optional `assetUrl`, tags). The human-written `description` is the grounding signal: a text model can't see the asset, so the "why it works" IS the inspiration; the asset is the visual shown in the library. - **Per-workspace RAG under commit `reference`** (`server/content/referenceLibrary.ts`) — mirrors brandMemory: one embedder, one `retrieve()`, indexed INCREMENTALLY (add → embed one row keyed by the example id; delete → remove that row). No global corpus (inspiration is the workspace's own). - **`generateScript` grounds on it**: retrieves the top-2 examples relevant to the brief and injects them as "Reference examples … emulate the APPROACH/structure, do NOT copy verbatim", alongside best-practices + brand. - **Ops** `reference-add`/`reference-delete` (content-* family, RBAC); the asset uploads via the existing media upload route → `assetUrl`. The snapshot exposes `content.references` for the library UI.

chunks.title: 0264-named-looks-in-agent-prompt
chunks.text: ADR 0264: 0264-named-looks-in-agent-prompt. The `design-system` context-doc the coding agent reads carried ONLY the active theme + style, so a ticket "build the dropdown in the Apple style" couldn't ground on Apple unless Apple was the active system. And the content-script prompt's best-practices/reference injection was retrieval-tested but the INJECTION itself was never asserted (stub mode discards the prompt). The user wants named references always available in prompts. Decision: - **A named-looks catalog in the design-system doc.** `buildDesignSystemDoc` now appends a catalog of every named look — the built-in premades (apple/material/…) AND the workspace's saved themes/styles — with each look's distinguishing tokens (primary/bg/text colours, radius, fonts, motion). So the agent can build in ANY named look, not just the active one. - **Premades come from a compiled JSON.** `scripts/generateDesignPremades.mjs` reads the client premade definitions (they only import types, so a tsx script can load them) → `docs/AI_DESIGN_PREMADES.json`, which the server reads. No client→server duplication; regenerate with `npm run ai:design-premades`. - **The doc exists from day one.** `rebuildDesignSystemDoc` is seeded on workspace creation and refreshed on every save/delete/setActive (not only setActive), so the named looks are available even before the user opens the Designer, and saved looks join/leave the catalog immediately. - **`generateScript.complete` is injectable** so a test captur

chunks.title: 0265-chat-op-catalog
chunks.text: ADR 0265: 0265-chat-op-catalog. The Workspace-AI could propose exactly 5 of the 138 control-ops (a hardcoded enum in `server/ai/workspaceChat.ts`) — the scan reports (SCAN_UNIVERSAL_TOOL / COMPLETENESS_SCAN) measured assistant-reachability at ~3.6% against the CLAUDE.md dual-mandate "every action via UI AND via the workspace-AI". The user decided (2026-07-09, UNIVERSAL_TOOL_PROGRAM §0): nearly ALL ops must become proposable, with destructive ones behind an extra explicit confirm. Decision: 1. **A single exhaustive op-catalog** (`server/ai/opCatalog.ts`, `Record<ControlOp, OpSpec>` — a missing op is a tsc error) classifies every op as `enabled` (proposable now + client-dispatchable), `later` (safe; flips to enabled when its dispatcher lands) or `excluded` (never via chat). 2. **Excluded forever:** secret-bearing ops (`save-env`, `save-integration`, `save-media-provider`, `gitlab-settings`, `forge-connect`, `db-connect`, `account-disconnect`) — secret values must never flow through the LLM/chat transcript — plus plumbing/legacy/dead ops (`create-workspace`, `accept-invite`, `accept-suggestion`, `mark-read`, `copilot-propose`, `answer-input`, `preview-up/down`, and the 5 ops the legacy rich chat path already covers). 3. **Generic validation before proposal:** params are spec-typed; workspace references (ticketKey/stageId/pieceId/envId/serviceName/preset) validate against the REAL context (`loadCtx` now also loads pieces/environments/services); undeclared fields are stripped. RBA

chunks.title: 0266-security-hardening-sweep
chunks.text: ADR 0266: 0266-security-hardening-sweep. The completeness/universal-tool scans surfaced a cluster of security defects (Rule 19). They fall in five groups: RBAC privilege-escalation (a `manageMembers`-only member could mint/assign admin-tier roles; the `promoteAdmin`/`demoteAdmin` capabilities were dead code; role perms had no ceiling and built-in roles were only client-locked), owner-protection (crafted sync-requests could re-role or remove the owner → dangling `ownerId`), a secret leak (internal `__`-prefixed EnvVars — provider API keys, OAuth-token JSON — were shipped in the workspace snapshot + Env tab and over the delta channel), a redacted-push regression (`PushSubscription.fullBodyOptIn` was stored but never read, so the full notification body always hit the lock screen despite the D80-reversed posture), a webhook SSRF hole (the trigger `webhook` action POSTed to any URL incl. loopback/metadata), a prod-deploy bypass (the direct prod Deploy button/op skipped the promote ladder's approval + green-CI + security gates), a missing confirm on the destructive `env-teardown`, a caller-scoping bug on single-notification mark-read, and the git clone/push token travelling in argv/URL. Decision: Fix all of them at the authoritative layer (the Conductor / server read-path / helpers), not the UI: - **SEC1** `change-role`: owner membership is never re-roled through this op; promoting INTO an admin-tier role requires `promoteAdmin`; re-roling a member who currently HOLDS an admin-tier

chunks.title: 0267-multi-repo-per-project-storage
chunks.text: ADR 0267: 0267-multi-repo-per-project-storage. `repoStore` keyed every on-disk git artifact by `workspaceId` alone: `data/workspaces/<ws>/repo.git` + `worktrees/` + `draft.Dockerfile`. A workspace can hold N `Project` rows (ADR 0035) and the metadata layer (project switcher, webhook routing by repo) supported them, but the physical storage did not — so **linking or greenfield-ing a 2nd project silently destroyed the 1st**: `cloneRepo` did `rmSync(bare)` before cloning, `initGreenfieldRepo` no-op'd when a bare repo already existed (2nd project got NO repo), worktrees were cut from the one shared clone, and `imageBuild`/`dockerfileGen` targeted `findFirst`-by-workspace (always the oldest project). This was the scan-flagged "R3-b" gap ("2nd repo overwrites the 1st"), deliberately deferred as too cross-cutting. Decision: Re-key ALL physical git storage by `(workspaceId, projectId)`: `data/workspaces/<ws>/projects/<proj>/{repo.git,worktrees/,draft.Dockerfile,merge-wt,revert-wt}`. - Every repo-touching `repoStore` function takes `projectId` (path helpers `projectDataDir`/ `bareRepoPath`/`worktreePath`; `cloneRepo`/`initGreenfieldRepo`/`addWorktree`/`repoStatus`/ `branchHead`/`branchDiff`/`mergeBranches`/`revertMergeCommit`/`listRepoFiles`/`repoHead`/ `showRepoFile`/`repoManifests`/`listRepoDocs`/`pushBranch`/`pushRef`/`isLinked`). - `cloneRepo` now `rmSync`-es only ITS OWN project slot; `initGreenfieldRepo` no-ops only when THAT project already has a repo — a sibling is never touch

chunks.title: 0268-multimodal-image-critique
chunks.text: ADR 0268: 0268-multimodal-image-critique. A headline media ask was "upload a photo and tell the AI what should change about it." The only existing "analyze" path (`analyzeReferenceVideo`) handed the media URL to the model as a TEXT string — the model never saw the pixels. No provider in the abstraction accepted image input. Decision: - **`AiCompletionRequest.imageUrls?: string[]`** — an optional multimodal input. The Gemini provider resolves each URL to bytes (local `/media/<file>` off the media store, or http fetch), base64-encodes it, and sends it as an `inline_data` part alongside the text prompt. Text-only providers (Claude CLI) ignore the field. Failed/oversized (>8MB) images are dropped so the turn still runs text-only. - **New `image-critique` AiFeature**, defaulted to `gemini-api` (vision-capable) in the assignment map; degrades to an honest stub without a key (never a fake result). - **`critiqueImage` service** + **`content-critique-image` control-op** (content family, RBAC `workTickets`): loads a ready IMAGE asset, runs the critique, stores the result on the asset's `metadata.critique` (+ `critiqueStub` honesty flag), and broadcasts a delta. **Advisory only** — it never edits the asset; the prompt maps each suggestion to an existing edit op (inpaint/adjust/crop/ regenerate) the user then runs. Reachable via the UI and (X1) proposable by the assistant. - **Lazy env read (bug fix):** the Gemini provider captured `GEMINI_API_KEY` at MODULE LOAD, but the key is a `@luck

chunks.title: 0269-channel-autopilot-consent-vooraf
chunks.text: ADR 0269: 0269-channel-autopilot-consent-vooraf. Invariant B-23 zegt: de mens keurt elke authoritative write goed; publiceren liep ALTIJD via een `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'publish')` die de gebruiker accepteert. Maar de productvisie ("10 YouTube-kanalen op cron-timers, een workspace puur voor automated content") vraagt een keten die zonder dagelijkse taps doorloopt: idee → render → publiceren. De gap-scan (GAP_SCAN_2026-07-16, critical "geen autonome end-to-end pipeline") bevestigde dat elke schakel handmatig was. De gebruiker heeft in het beslis-interview van 2026-07-17 expliciet gekozen voor per-kanaal opt-in. Decision: - **`Channel.autopilot` (default false)** is een per-kanaal opt-in die de gebruiker bewust aanzet via een expliciete confirm-dialoog. **Die consent vooraf ÍS de goedkeuring** voor elke publish vanaf dat kanaal — `content-request-publish` slaat de suggestion over en publiceert direct wanneer het kanaal autopilot aan heeft. chunks.text: ADR 0271: 0271-documents-module-markdown-bron-plus-render-targets. De gebruiker wil een volwaardige Documents-module (specs, plannen, briefings, sheets) waarin de AI alle bestandstypen kan maken en bewerken (Word/PDF/Excel/images), phone-first, met export. De bestaande content-pipeline is video/post-gericht; Studio-artifacts zijn campagne-gebonden. Er was geen generieke document-laag. chunks.title: 0273-comment-inbox-read-only-youtube-tiktok
chunks.text: ADR 0273: 0273-comment-inbox-read-only-youtube-tiktok. De gebruiker wil reacties op gepubliceerde posts kunnen ZIEN, per platform, phone-first — maar in het interview van 2026-07-17 expliciet gekozen: **alleen lezen, nog geen reply-opties** (geen AI-suggesties, geen autopilot-replies). Er bestond al: PublishJob met `externalId` (post-id), de OAuth-connectielaag met token-refresh, en het cron/metrics-ingest-patroon. Decision: Een `SocialComment`-cache (upsert op de platform-comment-id) gevoed door een refresh (cron `comments-ingest` elke WS_COMMENTS_INTERVAL_MIN + on-demand `comments-refresh`-op), per gekoppelde connectie over de done-posts. **Geen reply-surface** — het model heeft geen reply-veld, er is geen reply-op. chunks.title: 0274-pipeline-role-prompt-eval-replay-harness
chunks.text: ADR 0274: 0274-pipeline-role-prompt-eval-replay-harness. chunks.text: ADR 0275: 0275-voice-interface-provider-abstracted-stt-plus-tts. Feature-doc `06_VOICE_INPUT.md` ontwierp voice als BUILD-DEFERRED: self-hosted whisper.cpp, ALLEEN speech-to-text, geen TTS, met een streaming-upload-custom-route en drie send-to-targets. De user koos in het interview van 2026-07-17: voice bouwen, **provider-pluggable** STT/TTS, phone-first spraak-in voor de Assistant (PWA-mic → STT → bestaand chat-pad) én spraak-uit (TTS op antwoorden, opt-in). chunks.title: 0277-renewable-workspace-lease-with-fail-closed-guard
chunks.text: ADR 0277: 0277-renewable-workspace-lease-with-fail-closed-guard. ADR 0015 put the complete workspace-scoped Conductor critical section behind a fixed 15-second Redis lease, but did not renew it. If an action exceeded that TTL, a second instance could acquire the lease while the original callback kept running. The original caller could then complete successfully without observing that ownership had expired. Owner-checked release already prevented the stale owner from deleting its successor's lease, but it did not prevent or surface the overlapping work. ADR 0031 verified only short critical sections (60–80 ms) and leader exclusivity. Its broad conclusion that the engine was proven safe for N instances did not cover a greater-than-TTL action, lease loss mid-action, or cross-store fencing. Those claims must now be read through the limitations below. Decision: Workspace-scoped Conductor actions use a renewable owner-checked Redis lease and an explicit fail-closed lease guard; this strengthens mutual exclusion for normal asynchronous actions but is not database fencing. 1. `withWorkspaceLease` renews sequentially every 5 seconds for a 15-second TTL. The next renewal is not scheduled until the previous owner-checked renewal settles. Production timings stay fixed by default; the full timing set is injectable so real-Redis expiry tests run in hundreds of milliseconds. 2. chunks.text: ADR 0278: 0278-gap-scan-program-report-first-guards-and-additive-ops. The `GAP_SCAN_2026-07-17` audit produced ~37 open items spanning the autopilot chain, the phone-first approve/answer loop, eight orphaned couplings, reliability/observability, two security postures, content depth and six new modules. Delivering them raised three questions that recur across the whole program, and answering them once (here) is what keeps the individual changes consistent. Decision: **1. chunks.title: 0279-fenced-agent-recovery-writer
chunks.text: ADR 0279: 0279-fenced-agent-recovery-writer. chunks.text: ADR 0284: Blocked features explain themselves — a snapshot `readiness` block + resolved `myPerms` drive a permission-aware "what's missing / how to fix it" notice. Across the product many features silently do nothing until a precondition is met, and the failure was indistinguishable from "empty": - No git repo linked → the entire **Develop** module is dead (Code, containers, terminals, the AI coding agent all clone the repo), but the pages just showed a blank/ambiguous empty state. - No media-provider key → generation **"succeeds" with placeholder `stub://` assets** (the worst gate — it looks like it worked). - No AI provider (no Claude CLI on the host AND no Gemini key) → every AI feature returns nothing. - Docker down, no connected publish account, no encryption key → the same class of silent dead-end. chunks.text: ADR 0285: Every workspace write converges live for every room member via one Conductor-tail `workspaceDirty` broadcast. The goal: everything a user does is live for every other member of the same workspace, all small data is cached in memory (no re-GET on navigation), and big data (the codebase) is never preloaded. A four-agent scan found the architecture was **~85% there** already and named the exact gaps: - **Already correct:** exactly ONE socket.io room per workspace (`room == workspaceId`), every member joined for their whole session regardless of view; navigation derives `view` from the URL with no per-view GET; the snapshot preloads all small data for the active project; big data (repo tree, terminals, PTY, previews) stays lazy; cross-instance fan-out rides the Redis adapter. - **The core gap:** realtime coverage was **opt-in per entity**. Hot paths (tickets, content) broadcast their own targeted deltas, but ~25 COLD settings/infra control-ops ended in `syncRequest(...).then(refetch())` with no room broadcast — **only the initiator converged; every other member stayed stale until a manual reload**. A handful (`editSprint`, `reorderStages`, `saveGitlab`, `copyWorkspaceAssets`) didn't even refetch for the initiator. New ops kept falling into the same trap because nothing generalized the pattern. chunks.title: Switching workspace/project is instant via a client stale-while-revalidate snapshot cache + idle prefetch
chunks.text: ADR 0286: Switching workspace/project is instant via a client stale-while-revalidate snapshot cache + idle prefetch. ADR 0285 made every write live for the ACTIVE workspace and confirmed the snapshot preloads all small data for the active workspace + active project (so the first board visit is instant). One gap remained (P5): the snapshot is scoped to ONE active project, so switching project — or workspace — threw away the whole `snap` and re-pulled everything (a ~60–80 query build) behind a loading state. No switch was ever instant after the first, and returning to a workspace you were just on still spun.
