chunks.title: Host administration, workspace governance, and browser terminals are separate fail-closed security planes
chunks.text: ADR 0287: Host administration, workspace governance, and browser terminals are separate fail-closed security planes. The application had three authority leaks: 1. Workspace owner/admin terminology was being treated as a possible future host-admin shortcut even though membership is tenant-scoped. A self-host operator needs a separate global role. 2. The browser terminal still had a development fallback that spawned a shell in the application/host process, and its container mode trusted a client-provided Docker name after checking only that it had *some* Workspaces label. The ticket detail panel omitted the name and therefore selected the host fallback. 3. Member governance had coarse checks: accepting a workspace suggestion was marked login-only; a manageMembers role could invite/remove built-in admins; `ownerActions` on a custom role could reach ownership transfer; repeated invite/suggestion actions were not uniformly idempotent. Decision: - The framework-global `User.admin` field means **host superadmin only**. It is never inferred from `WorkspaceMember.roleKey`. Workspace `owner`/`admin` remains full authority only within that workspace. Root operators can bootstrap/recover the host role with `WS_SUPERADMIN_EMAILS`; all host-plane routes must use the shared `isHostSuperadmin`/`assertHostSuperadmin` guard. A host superadmin does not implicitly become a workspace member either. - Browser terminals are **container-only in every environment**. The host-shell backend and its env

chunks.title: Unrestricted Docker Compose runs only on an external per-workspace sandbox
chunks.text: ADR 0288: Unrestricted Docker Compose runs only on an external per-workspace sandbox. The product must support arbitrary third-party Docker Compose, not only curated presets. The prior YAML sanitizer rejected privileged mode and obvious binds, but missed parts of long syntax and can never make every future Compose/Docker feature safe. Conversely, allowing those directives on the application daemon gives a workspace user root-equivalent access to the Workspaces host. Project-name/network prefixes also do not stop cross-tenant access on one daemon. Decision: - Production never runs workspace Compose on the app Docker daemon. It calls a root-configured HTTPS runner URL containing `{workspaceId}`; each resolved endpoint represents a dedicated VM/microVM/physical sandbox. - Inside that sandbox Compose is unrestricted. Workspaces preserves the raw YAML instead of pretending a sanitizer is the security boundary. - The runner returns explicit gateway/overlay environment values for services needed by app/agent containers; Workspaces never assumes same-daemon DNS. - Missing/invalid runner configuration fails closed in production. Restricted local sanitization remains only as a development fallback. - Conductor owns desired-state persistence and records which backend must handle teardown.

chunks.title: Conductor route-write migration seam
chunks.text: ADR 0289: Conductor route-write migration seam. Several authenticated `_api` routes predated the control-API split and still mutated Prisma or repository files directly. Moving account, PAT, Studio, AI-chat and file writes into new public control verbs would expand the frozen structured surface and expose route-internal operations to the Assistant. Holding the workspace lease around Studio generation, documentation generation or Docker image builds would block unrelated writes for seconds or minutes. Decision: Legacy route-internal writes use `enqueueWorkspaceRouteWrite` or `enqueueGlobalRouteWrite`. Workspace writes execute under the cross-instance workspace lease, writer context and `runInTenant`; global account writes execute on the global writer chain. Slow AI/provider/image-build work runs before the lease, followed by a short completion write through the seam. Worktree writes re-check the stage edit lock inside that lease. This is explicitly a migration seam, not the target for new domain operations. It appends an audit signal, but arbitrary callbacks are not reconstructable after a process crash. New durable domain work continues to use typed `ControlOp`/`InternalOp`; remaining callback users must migrate to typed replayable jobs before the seam can claim crash durability.

chunks.title: Tenant-scoped proxy, media and egress boundaries
chunks.text: ADR 0290: Tenant-scoped proxy, media and egress boundaries. Ticket keys, branch names and service names are unique only inside a workspace. Using those values as global proxy ids/hosts allowed one tenant's upsert to replace another tenant's route. Unsigned media reads required membership in any workspace rather than ownership of the file's workspace. Worker egress confinement was opt-in and could be bypassed by later attaching the worker to a normal proxy network. Decision: Generated preview, ref-preview, editor and environment route ids/hosts include the workspace id. Custom domains and subdomains are globally collision-checked. Edge auth continues to resolve host ownership through Redis and requires the route workspace's capability. New local media files receive a filesystem ownership sidecar when promoted or generated. Unsigned downloads require membership in that exact workspace; legacy generated files may resolve ownership only through tenant-bearing database rows. Valid short-lived HMAC links remain the deliberate cookie-less path for publishing platforms and public pages. Production defaults `WS_EGRESS` to enforcement. Any secondary network attached to a confined worker must be Docker-internal; an existing externally routed proxy network fails closed. The production bootstrap creates `workspaces-net` as internal.

chunks.title: Budgeted capability-aware Workspace-AI tools
chunks.text: ADR 0291: Budgeted capability-aware Workspace-AI tools. The Workspace-AI catalog had 148 nominally enabled actions and injected all enabled-module hints into every turn. This consumed context, advertised actions the caller could not authorize, and encouraged semantically weak tool selection. Workspace instructions and enabled skills had no aggregate hard ceiling, so user-managed context could crowd out the feature contract and current request. Decision: The catalog remains exhaustive for validation and client dispatch; no verb is added or removed from the frozen surface. For a real chat request, the server filters actions by enabled module, the caller's effective capability vector and availability of every required entity reference. It then ranks the remaining hints against the request and exposes at most 36. Every one-shot AI feature passes through a provider-independent 64,000-character central budget at `runAiCompletion`: 20,000 current-prompt characters, 32,000 feature-system characters, 4,000 workspace instruction characters, 6,000 skill characters and 2,000 product-capability characters. Truncation is explicit and preserves both the beginning and end of a section.

chunks.title: Typed route jobs use bounded replay and runtime claims
chunks.text: ADR 0292: Typed route jobs use bounded replay and runtime claims. ADR 0289 moved legacy route callbacks under the Conductor, but their closures could not be reconstructed after a process crash. Studio generation, docs/image completion, chat persistence, design-library writes, PAT issuance, file saves and editor/preview launches therefore had writer serialization without durable replay. Slow Docker/proxy work also could not remain inside the workspace lease. A naive replay of every persisted payload is unsafe: an old file, brand/style import or completion can overwrite a newer authoritative write. A periodic runtime sweep can also duplicate a launch that is merely slow rather than crashed. Decision: Workspace route writes use bounded, runtime-validated `InternalOp` payloads persisted in `WorkspaceSignal`. Deterministic Mongo IDs make create-style effects idempotent. The leader recovery sweep reconstructs only an explicit allowlist of idempotent operations and compares entity replay keys against later processed internal signals; a superseded signal is acknowledged without applying its stale payload. File and brand/style operations remain auditable typed signals but are excluded from crash replay until they gain an entity CAS/version that also covers out-of-band writers. Editor, preview, ref-preview and preview-close use a durable prepare → external execute → typed completion protocol. Docker/proxy execution stays outside the workspace writer lease. A per-intent Redis lease prev

chunks.title: Workspace-AI has no ambiguous later operations
chunks.text: ADR 0293: Workspace-AI has no ambiguous later operations. The exhaustive Workspace-AI catalog still classified seven operations as `later`. That state did not tell users or maintainers whether an operation lacked wiring, duplicated another verb, needed unavailable context or was intentionally outside the workspace assistant boundary. Leaving entries ambiguous also allowed future work to mistake catalog presence for an executable effect. Decision: The catalog has only `enabled` and `excluded` outcomes. `db-migrate-apply` is enabled because an existing pending migration can be validated from tenant-scoped context, dispatched through the existing project-admin sync route and protected by destructive confirmation plus the route's own approval/environment gates. The other six operations are excluded: - `gitlab-verify` duplicates the real credential-free resync/connectivity path and its legacy handler is a no-op. - `raise-cap` aliases canonical `edit-budget`. - `content-create` duplicates the richer brief-based content creation path. - `content-reorder-beats` and `content-save-scenes` require a complete destructive timeline graph that is intentionally owned by the visual editor. - `copy-workspace-assets` crosses workspace boundaries and remains an explicit UI flow where both memberships can be shown and confirmed.

chunks.title: Move cheap-mode, scene-continuity and default TTS voice from host env to per-workspace media prefs
chunks.text: ADR 0294: Move cheap-mode, scene-continuity and default TTS voice from host env to per-workspace media prefs. Several media-generation knobs were host-global env-only (`WS_MEDIA_CHEAP`, `WS_SCENE_CONTINUITY`, `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID`), so one deployment could not vary them per tenant even though media provider keys and per-feature model overrides already resolve per workspace (ADR 0086/0091/0110/0111) via the encrypted `EnvVar __`-namespace store + `loadWorkspaceMediaConfig` (env as fallback). The owner asked to pull "as many env settings as sensibly possible" into the per-workspace environment. The question was where the three workspace-wide (not per-feature) media defaults should live and how they get written, without adding to the assistant's frozen verb surface (invariant 2). Decision: Store the three as workspace-wide plaintext `EnvVar` rows in the same `__`-namespace the media config loader already reads: `__media_cheap` (`'1'`), `__media_scene_continuity` (`'on'`), `__media_voice_id` (a public voice id, not a secret). `loadWorkspaceMediaConfig` reads them; `runMediaGeneration` layers them UNDER the caller's `params` (a per-request param always wins) as `params.cheap` / `params.voiceId`, and `sceneDecompose` ORs the per-workspace flag with the env default. They are WRITTEN through the EXISTING `save-media-provider` control-API op — presence-based, so sending only one pref leaves the others (and provider keys/models) untouched — surfaced in the snapshot as `content.mediaPre

chunks.title: Consolidate semantic duplicates, not domain history
chunks.text: ADR 0295: Consolidate semantic duplicates, not domain history. The audit found two actual skill stores: instruction skills in `Skill` and workflow capabilities in `InfoSource(mode='skill')`. It also found similarly named brand/style, document/RAG and artifact models. Those latter groups are not interchangeable rows: they represent source versus derived index, identity versus generation preset, or separate lifecycle/retention domains. ADR 0034 already rejected a single artifact mega-table and ADR 0270 kept instruction skills, styles and design artifacts semantically separate. Decision: `Skill` is the one skill store. `skillType='instruction'` rows contain reusable prompt instructions; `skillType='capability'` rows retain workflow-tool metadata (`kind`, `model`, `projectId`, `usedByStages`, status/description). Watermarked schema step 6 creates a capability row with `legacyInfoSourceId` before deleting each legacy `InfoSource(mode='skill')`. The frozen `skill-toggle` operation still accepts `sourceId`: it toggles a capability Skill first and falls back to a context-document InfoSource, so no public verb or client contract changes. The other models remain intentionally layered: - `Document` is mutable source, `DocumentRevision` is history, and `RagEntry` is a rebuildable derived retrieval index. - `StudioBrandLibrary` is workspace brand identity; `StylePreset` is a per-feature generation preset. - `DesignArtifact`, `StudioArtifact`, `BuildArtifact`, `ContentAsset` and document e

chunks.title: Global writes use encrypted durable Conductor jobs
chunks.text: ADR 0296: Global writes use encrypted durable Conductor jobs. ADR 0289 serialized account/global route callbacks only in one process. A crash lost the callback, multiple app instances had separate global chains, and persisting Web Push keys or import bundles as plaintext replay payloads would create a second sensitive-data store. Workspace import was additionally non-idempotent: retrying after a partial create could produce another workspace. Decision: Global route writes use the closed `GlobalAction` union and `GlobalJob` collection. The full validated payload is AES-256-GCM encrypted with `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY`; searchable columns contain only job identity, kind, owner, status and retry metadata. Deterministic action hashing supplies the job ID and dedup key. Recovery replays only the typed union, with five bounded attempts. Typed global jobs and login-only global control actions share one renewable Redis lease (`global`) and the explicit global writer context. Account updates, preferences, account deletion, SSH add/remove, Push save/remove, PAT revoke and workspace import no longer accept callback writers. Session bearer tokens are never stored in a job. User rows are authoritative; the requesting route refreshes its derived session cache after job completion. Workspace import uses a deterministic workspace ID and an `importCompleted` marker. A partial import is deleted and rebuilt; a completed retry returns the same workspace.

chunks.title: Compose runner uses one Proxmox QEMU sandbox per workspace
chunks.text: ADR 0297: Compose runner uses one Proxmox QEMU sandbox per workspace. ADR 0288 requires unrestricted user-supplied Docker Compose to leave the Workspaces application daemon and run inside a dedicated VM/microVM/physical sandbox per workspace. The application-side HTTPS contract existed, but there was no deployable control-plane, sandbox lifecycle or selected hypervisor. A Docker sidecar or shared remote daemon would still give one tenant root-equivalent access to other tenants. Decision: - The first production runner backend is **Proxmox VE with a full-cloned QEMU VM per workspace**. Proxmox VM configuration is the durable identity/state source; the runner remains stateless and reconstructs ownership from a marker plus the exact workspace id in the VM description. - A separately deployed HTTPS control-plane authenticates the Workspaces bearer token, verifies URL/body workspace equality, serializes operations per workspace, provisions/reuses the VM and forwards only to that VM's agent. - A host-level systemd agent inside the disposable VM executes raw Compose. Its bearer token is HMAC-derived per workspace and injected after clone over a restricted cloud-init SSH principal; the public runner token is never forwarded into a sandbox. - Isolation is enforced outside the guest by Proxmox firewall rules: deny-by-default ingress, agent access only from controller CIDRs, explicitly labelled gateway ports only from Workspaces app CIDRs, and private/metadata egress denial before public
